## 7 Reasons Why You Should Insulate Your Roof Before Winters
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/7-reasons-why-you-should-insulate-your-roof-before-winters/
Updated: 2025-10-24
Summary: Learn why insulating your roof before winter is essential for energy efficiency, comfort, and saving on heating costs.

7 Reasons Why You Should Insulate Your Roof Before Winters
Oct 30, 2024
Winters can be unforgiving, especially when your home lacks proper insulation. But before that, what does insulation mean? It is a material that helps prevent heat from transmitting from one area to another. The most common insulation materials include cellulose, fiberglass, and foam, and can be available in batts, fill, rolls, and spray boards. Keep on reading to learn why you should insulate your roof before winters.
Reasons To Replace Your Roof Insulation
Replacing your roof insulation before winter starts can have many advantages, including:
Lower Energy Bills
If your home has old or outdated insulation, it is confirmed that you will receive higher utility bills. Replacing your roof insulation can lower this number by minimizing energy loss through your roof. Other factors can also influence this, such as your lifestyle, type of heating system, home design, and size of your roof’s.
Maintain a Safe Home Structure
A newly replaced roof insulation can also result in a safer home structure. For instance, if you live in an area that is prone to high moisture, vapors can gradually seep into the house, deteriorating its material integrity and structure. Insulation acts as a moisture deterrent. Especially during winter, it can prevent ice dams that may cause wood rot, mold, and other issues.
Better Indoor Air Quality
A properly insulated roof can also positively impact your home’s air quality. If there are no air leaks, dirt, dust, mildew, and other contaminants will be less likely to enter your house. This will result in a cleaner indoor environment, allowing your loved ones to breathe clean, dirt-free air.
Less Wear & Tear On HVAC Systems
A new heating system is relatively expensive, so homeowners tend to find ways to extend their lives through regular maintenance. One thing to note here is that failing to properly insulate your roof or its attic can put extra stress on your HVAC system. When your unit is made to work harder, it reduces its lifespan, necessitating an upgrade every few years. Replacing your roof and attic insulation can be the best way to ease stress on your HVAC system.
Protecting The Environment
By replacing your roof insulation , you are also favoring the environment. It saves energy, which is good for the environment. The total amount of energy we consume can affect the entire ecosystem. You can play your part to help the environment by doing the needful.
Better Noise Reduction
Roof insulation reduces indoor noise levels. Insulation materials absorb outdoor sounds, ensuring they do not hinder living space. This proves that roof insulation can positively impact your living standards if you reside in a noisy neighborhood, especially in winter when outdoor noises amplify.
Increased Indoor Comfort
A cool draft of air can compromise indoor comfort. Properly insulated roofs can ensure otherwise. Insulation can protect cool air to enter the house while making sure that warm air does not leave also.
Final Words
Roof insulation counts as a major home improvement project. It can contribute to lower energy bills, less wear and tear on HVAC systems, protecting the environment, better noise reduction and increased indoor comfort. ## 8 Signs Your Gutter Needs Cleaning
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/8-signs-your-gutter-needs-cleaning/
Updated: 2025-10-24
Summary: Overflowing water, sagging gutters, or plant growth? These are signs your gutters need cleaning. Get expert tips from Everest Siding & Windows

8 Signs Your Gutter Needs Cleaning
Jun 15, 2025
Gutters are an important part of your home. But most often, their cleaning and maintenance are overlooked until they start causing problems. Dirty gutters are not only an aesthetic concern but also lead to structural and health issues.
In this blog, we will discuss 8 signs that indicate your gutter needs professional cleaning.
Signs Your Gutter Needs Professional Cleaning
Listed below are 8 signs that indicate the dire need for professional gutter cleaning :
1. Overflowing Water
Gutters are supposed to drain water away from your house. One of the most crucial signs that your gutter needs cleaning is overflowing water during a rainstorm. This is a sign that your gutter is clogged, preventing water from flowing freely, causing spills.
2. Visible Debris
Again, the most prominent and visible sign indicating the need for professional gutter cleaning is debris accumulation. Debris in the form of leaves, twigs, or dust can cause buildup, which leads to clogged gutters, preventing proper water drainage and potentially leading to water damage to roofs, walls, and ceilings.
3. Pests and Animals around Gutters
Mosquitoes, rodents, and birds are attracted to clogged gutters, which act as a favorable breeding ground for these creatures. If you notice an unusual increase in pests around your gutters, it is a sign that they need to be cleaned right away.
4. Sagging Gutters
When gutters get clogged with leaves and water, they become heavy. This extra weight can make them sag or pull away from the house. If you see this happening, it’s a sign they need to be cleaned and maybe fixed.
5. Plant Growth
If you see plants or weeds growing in your gutters, it means that they are clogged. Leaves and dirt can build up and create a place where seeds can grow. Greenery in the gutters is a clear sign that they need to be cleaned.
6. Mold and Mildew
The presence of mold and mildew is another sign that you must hire professional gutter cleaning services. When water can’t flow properly, it overflows and keeps the area damp, which helps mold grow. This is a serious health and hygiene risk that needs to be taken care of immediately.
7. Water Damage
Water backups from clogged gutters can overflow and seep into your roof, ceilings, or even foundation. This can cause serious damage to your home over time. Cleaning your gutters professionally, every once in a while, helps avoid these costly problems.
8. Roof Leaks
When gutters are clogged with debris, water cannot flow away properly. Instead, it can back up onto the roof. Over time, this standing water can seep under shingles or damage the roof edge, leading to leaks inside your home.
Overall Insight
Dirty and clogged gutters are a serious concern. They not only pose structural risks but also create health and safety risks for your family. Some common signs that indicate your gutter needs professional cleaning are overflowing water, visible debris, pests, mold, plant growth, sagging gutters, water damage, and roof leaks.
Looking for professional gutter cleaning services in Houston, TX? Call Everest Siding and Windows at (832) 334-2528 to schedule your preferred date.

## A Guide to Increasing Home Value with Outdoor Living Spaces
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/a-guide-to-increasing-home-value-with-outdoor-living-spaces/
Updated: 2026-05-13
Summary: Are you thinking of making improvements to your outdoor living space? Discover how outdoor living enhances your home’s worth.

A Guide to Increasing Home Value with Outdoor Living Spaces
Apr 30, 2026
Upgrading outdoor living spaces is a reliable way to increase home value. Functional areas for relaxation and entertainment improve a property’s appeal and usability. This guide explains how outdoor living enhances your home’s worth. It also shows how to get the most money back by choosing the right upgrades.
Why Does Outdoor Living Enhancement Increase Your Home Value?
Our daily life is busy, and everyone needs a place to relax and connect with nature. A well-designed backyard or front yard provides this space. Choosing the right exterior features can transform your yard into a functional space for relaxation and recreation.
For example, adding a patio, an outdoor kitchen, or a garden makes the home more functional. These upgrades increase market value and attract more buyers.
What Are the Key Features That Boost Your Outdoor Living Space?
If you have decided to enhance your outdoor living space, and you are considering what to add to make it functional for yourself or for the buyers. Here are a few ideas;
Patios and Decks
Patios and decks are essential outdoor features. They create a defined outdoor space for dining, seating, and entertaining. They also make your living space bigger without the need for major construction, which makes them a cost-effective upgrade.
Outdoor Shade Structures
Shades like pergolas, covered patios, and awnings make outdoor spaces more usable and comfortable. They help shield from the sun and from mild rain, allowing homeowners to use them for longer periods throughout the season. Adding shade turns a previously exposed zone into a usable seating or dining area.
Outdoor Lighting
Outdoor lighting adds purpose to your outdoor living space, allowing you to utilize patios, decks, and walkways long after dark. Enhancing visibility and reducing the risk of accidents. As lighting highlights areas, like seating space, plants, and pathways.
Outdoor Kitchens and Dining Areas
Outdoor kitchens and dining areas give you a place to cook, eat, and have fun outside. which makes the kitchen experience better. Outdoor kitchens typically include built-in grills, countertops, storage, and seating, making them highly functional.
Landscaping and Greenery
Landscaping makes your outdoor living space more beautiful and functional. The mix of plants, lawns, trees, and garden designs enhances curb appeal and creates a welcoming atmosphere.
Fire Features
Fire pits and outdoor fireplaces provide warmth and comfort. These features create a central gathering spot where families and guests can relax. They also extend the usefulness of your yard into the evening when temperatures drop.
How Does It Improve Your Return On Investment?
Upgrading outdoor living spaces increases a home’s market value. Many buyers prefer move-in-ready houses because they reduce the need for future projects. These improvements can lead to higher offers and a faster sale in the real estate market.
To Sum It Up
Outdoor living improvements increase a home’s value by making it more attractive and functional, which makes it desirable to buyers. If you want to upgrade your outdoor space, feel free to reach out to Everest Siding and Windows.

## After The Storm: 3 Reasons You Need To Inspect Your Roof
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/after-the-storm-3-reasons-you-need-to-inspect-your-roof/
Updated: 2024-12-23
Summary: After the recent storms that have pelted the Houston area you’ve probably noticed a dozen signs for Houston roofing companies.

After The Storm: 3 Reasons You Need To Inspect Your Roof
Aug 26, 2019
After the recent storms that have pelted the Houston area you’ve probably noticed a dozen signs for Houston roofing companies. If you haven’t already checked out your roof don’t put it off. With the high winds, heavy rainfall and hail that has come down, your roof might have damage you don’t see right away. Just because damage to your roof hasn’t manifested itself in the form of leaks, doesn’t mean that damage can’t turn into a huge mess if left untreated. Roofs aren’t cheap and inspecting your roof after a storm could save you thousands. Do we have your attention now? Good.
Early Detection Is Key
If your roof has been compromised and become vulnerable to leaking, in most cases catching it early and contain the damage. In most cases, once you correct the damage early you prevent any physical leaks from even occurring. Most homeowners headaches happen when they just assume the roof is ok because there are no leaks in the ceiling. They let problems fester undetected and then, what could’ve been a $600.00 repair turns into a roof replacement that costs thousands of dollars. That alone could save you thousands and keep your insurance rates down.
Insurance Has Limits
If your home did actually suffer storm damage and you failed to detect it until several months later, your insurance company likely may decline to cover it. Many insurance companies have time limits on filing a claim built into their policies. The best practice is to contact a Houston roofing company the day after a bad storm and inspect your roof. If there is damage catching it early gives you the chance to document evidence for your insurance claim. This is especially helpful if you have an aging roof that is already old if you get storm damage evidence documented, well you just saved yourself thousands because the insurance will cover it now.
It Costs You Nothing
The fact is most Houston roofing companies will inspect your roof for free. Think about it, if they inspect it and nothing is wrong they’ve made a customer contact and their name is in your memory for the future. It is a win-win for them and a loss leader to generate more business. For you, it gives you the peace of mind if there is nothing wrong, and gives you the jump on the situation if there is. Just make sure the company you choose is reputable, check out their reviews on the internet and that they are bonded and insured. Most reputable Houston roofing companies will show you their bonding upfront and be transparent with the inspection process.
Call The Best At Everest
Now that you really have no excuse to have your roof inspected, it’s time to call Everest and schedule a free inspection of your roof. Our qualified roofing experts will come to your home and give you a fair and honest inspection and a quote for repair costs if needed.

## Are Energy Efficient Windows Worth It?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/are-energy-efficient-windows-worth-it/
Updated: 2024-12-24
Summary: Discover the benefits of energy-efficient windows, their cost savings, and if they're the right investment for your home.

Are Energy Efficient Windows Worth It?
Aug 26, 2019
Energy Efficient windows provide many benefits for you and your family. Not only do you save money by using less energy but they add to your personal comfort as well. In the Houston, TX area annual energy savings by installing energy efficient windows ranges from 17 to 31%. While you are saving money, you’re also benefitting the environment.
How do they work?
Shielding you from the heat in the summer and the bitter cold in the winter, energy efficient windows ensure that you’re comfortable all year round. Since the interior glass is designed to block out the outside temperature, the window stays warm in the winter, blocking out drafts and cool in the summer, blocking out the heat. Additionally, these windows protect your valuables from fading as they are designed to block out harmful ultraviolet rays without reducing visible light.
Fringe Benefit
One of the most beneficial and often overlooked benefits of having energy efficient windows is that they are excellent at reducing unwanted noises like trains, sirens, and traffic. This is a desirable feature especially in today’s communities where homes are often very close to one another.
How do I get started?
To acquire more information about energy efficient vinyl windows, contact Everest Siding and Windows today to set up a no-obligation on-site consultation. Our team of professionals is dedicated to helping you save money and live more comfortably. We’re ready when you are!

## Buyers Guide to exterior siding
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/buyers-guide-to-exterior-siding/
Updated: 2025-10-02
Summary: Explore our buyer's guide to exterior siding and learn about materials, installation, and maintenance for your home.

Buyers Guide to exterior siding
Aug 26, 2019
Buyers guide to exterior siding
Your home exterior is one of the most important barriers that protect your home, your valuables inside, and your love ones from heat, wind, rain, and other hazards. Therefore, it is important to choose a product that will guarantee the security and durability you and your family need. Siding replacement provides great opportunity to add color, definition, and character to your home, plus provides a major upgrade in your home’s appearance and value— that’s the fun part. On the flip side, it’s not an easy decision to make. There are lots of siding options, and each presents a mixed bag of cost, reliability, ongoing maintenance, and environmental responsibility. While aesthetics are always important, you may want to consider the material’s durability, ability to resist water, ease of installation and versatility. Here’s what you should know about today’s most popular options when it comes to improving your home exterior:
Engineered Wood Siding
Engineered wood siding is made of wood fibers and exterior-grade resins. It’s tough, strong and can stand up to extreme weather conditions. It comes in a variety of styles and textures, including beaded lap, rough-sawn clapboard and look-alike wood shingles. It comes ready-to-paint, primed or with factory finishes.Engineered wood siding positions itself as a lower cost alternative to fiber cement and real wood, but with similar durability. LP SmartSide brand provides 50-year warranties.Upside: Easy to work, with no harmful dust. Borate compounds added to the mixture make engineered wood siding impervious to insects. It’s half the cost of real wood siding.
Downside:
Because LP® SmartSide® is a wood based product similar to Masonite it is not resistant to woodpeckers.
Green meter:
Binders are low-VOC. Manufacturing uses entire trees and select wood scrap so that production waste is minimal.
Cost:
$5 to $8 per square foot, installed. Expect to pay $8,000 to $13,000 to cover an average two-story house. Learn more about it.
Wood Siding
Commonly used for bungalow, Cape Cod and cottage exteriors, wood siding offers a rich look and is durable if maintained properly. This siding option has great aesthetics, but keep in mind that it requires periodic maintenance (caulking and painting or staining to prevent weather damage) and is susceptible to insect, rodent, and critters.Wood siding comes in clapboard (also known as lap or bevel siding) as well as shakes and shingles. Clapboard siding uses planks of wood installed horizontally with an upper piece that overlaps the lower piece. Western red cedar and redwood, woods known for being attractive and durable, are considered the best choices.More uniform in appearance but thinner than shakes, shingles give you a smooth and consistent look. They can be cut into different shapes to add visual interest to your exterior. Some manufacturers also offer shingles treated with fire-retardant chemicals, often a requirement in high-risk locations. Be sure to check into the local regulations in your area.If you do the maintenance right, wood siding can last from 10 to 100 years. Clear finishes should be reapplied every two years; semi-transparent stains every three years; and paints every five years. That kind of diligence adds up — a complete refinishing job is $2,000 to $5,000 on an average size home.
Upside:
Wood is easy to cut and shape, and can be installed by reasonably skilled DIYers. It’s a great-looking material prized by architects, designers and homeowners for its natural beauty.
Better grades of wood can be pricey. Diligent maintenance adds to the overall cost. Retrofitting with wood siding requires removing existing siding materials.
Wood siding is considered a highly sustainable material that breaks down easily in landfills. The best grades are made from old-growth timber
$5 to $10 per square foot, installed. Expect to pay $14,000 to $28,000 to have wood siding professionally installed on an average two-story house.
Fiber Cement
Offering the look of masonry, stucco or wood at a lower cost, fiber-cement siding has become a popular siding choice for many homeowners. Fiber-cement siding is low-maintenance, non-flammable and termite-resistant. Available in a range of styles and textures, factory painting or finishes are available.On the other side, fiber-cement siding could encounter possible moisture-related problems, and older homes built before the late 1980s may have siding that contains asbestos and requires a professional abatement contractor for removal.Depending on the manufacturer, the fiber cement siding will last 20 to 30 years. The current darling of the siding industry, fiber cement has earned a reputation for stability and low maintenance. It’s made from a mix of wood pulp, cement, clay and sand, and it can be molded to mimic wood clapboard, shingles, stucco and masonry. It readily accepts paint, and most manufacturers offer an array of factory-applied finishes.
Fiber-cement siding resists expanding and contracting with changes in humidity and temperature, so caulk and paint really hold up. It’s fire-resistant, termite-proof and it won’t rot. A 30-year warranty is the norm.
Fiber-cement siding is flat-out heavy, and installation requires special techniques and tools that add to the cost. It should be installed by a trained professional. There are specific guidelines that need to be followed to make sure this product lasts.
It’s extremely durable and has a long replacement cycle, which scores points for sustainability.
$8 to $13 per square foot, installed (cost higher with trim). Expect to pay $20,000 to $32,500 for an average two-story house. Read more about it.
Vinyl
The low cost, versatility and easy maintenance of vinyl siding has helped it become the most popular siding choice in the United States. While some design professionals and homeowners are turned off by the “plastic look” of some vinyl siding products, the variety of colors and styles available helps explain this siding’s popularity.Requiring few tools to install and available at home improvement stores, this is an option for those looking for a do-it-yourself product. Since mistakes can be costly, make sure to follow instructions from the manufacturer and take advantage of online how-to videos.Vinyl siding is tough and comes in a boatload of colors and textures. Because the color is throughout the material, nicks and scratches don’t show up. Sophisticated manufacturing techniques create products that do a surprisingly fine job of mimicking wood-grain lap siding, wood shingles and even stone.Vinyl siding is lightweight and, in many instances, can be installed directly over existing materials, so it’s a good retrofit option. Because it’s easy to handle, vinyl installation can be installed quickly, saving labor costs.Relatively new to the market, insulated vinyl siding features a layer of expanded polystyrene foam, providing an insulating value of R-2 to R-6. Insulated vinyl is on the checklist of items that can help a house achieve Energy Star qualification. Expect to pay about 15 percent more for insulated versions of vinyl siding than regular.
The material requires little or no maintenance, and dirt simply washes off. Never needs repainting. Vinyl has relatively low cost compared to other siding materials. The best brands offer transferable lifetime warranties.
Because the standard panels are 12 feet long, the ends of the panels must be overlapped, creating noticeable seams. You can order extra-long panels that reduce the number of seams, but you’ll pay a premium of about 30 percent more than standard-length vinyl.
The same stuff that makes vinyl so tough — polyvinyl chloride or PVC — lasts for decades (if not centuries) in landfills. Although many vinyl manufacturers claim that the material is readily recycled, not many contractors take the time to remove and recycle used vinyl siding. Manufacturing PVC can produce dioxin and

## Can Clogged Gutters Damage Your Roof?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/can-clogged-gutters-damage-your-roof/
Updated: 2026-06-08
Summary: Are you seeing sagging shingles or ceiling stains? Your gutters might be clogged. Learn how to stop gutter-related roof damage before it worsens.

Can Clogged Gutters Damage Your Roof?
May 30, 2026
Your roof keeps your home dry, but stuck leaves can ruin the entire system. Most homeowners don’t notice a problem until they see sagging shingles or ceiling stains. Learning how clogged gutters damage your roof stops these disasters early.
Let’s look at how a simple clog turns into a major repair and how you can protect your house.
How Do Clogged Gutters Damage Roof Boards?
When gutters stay full, water sits right against the edge of your roof. This trapped moisture eventually seeps into the wooden fascia boards that support your gutters. Since wet wood rots fast, the boards get soft and cannot hold the heavy gutters anymore.
Full gutters force water to back up and seep under your shingles. This moisture hits the wooden roof deck and stays there. Over time, this can lead to mold growth and interior ceiling stains.
How Do Blocked Gutters Lead to Ice Dams in Winter?
In colder climates, blocked gutters contribute to the formation of ice dams. When snow melts and hits the cold clogged gutter, it refreezes at the roof’s edge. This ice forces water upward under the shingles, causing significant leaks that are very difficult to fix in winter.
The purpose of a gutter system is to direct rainwater far away from the building walls. When the troughs overflow, water pours down the siding and collects at the base of the home. Regular gutter cleaning ensures water moves away so the soil does not shift and crack the foundation.
Can Heavy Debris Cause Gutters to Collapse?
Wet leaves and silt are incredibly heavy. A gutter filled with sludge puts immense physical strain on the brackets holding it to your home. Eventually, the gutters may pull away entirely, ripping off the fascia board and damaging the roof’s perimeter in a single sudden collapse.
Stagnant water in a blocked gutter is a breeding ground for mosquitoes, carpenter ants, and even rodents. These pests eventually move from the gutters into your attic space through the rotted wood. Maintaining clear channels discourages these infestations and keeps your home’s attic much safer and drier.
How Does Regular Gutter Cleaning Extend Roof Life?
The best way to protect your investment is through consistent maintenance and observation. Clearing out the debris twice a year ensures that rainwater moves freely. By keeping the drainage clear, you extend the life of your shingles and avoid the headache of a premature roof replacement.
You should also inspect the downspouts to ensure water is actually exiting the system. Sometimes the top opening is clear, but a blockage deep inside the pipe causes a backup. Keeping the entire path open protects the roof edges from rot and keeps the wood dry.
Bottom Line
Keeping your gutters clear is the best way to protect your roof and foundation from water damage. Don’t wait for a leak to start before taking action. For professional help with your home’s exterior, reach out to Everest Siding and Windows at (832) 334-2528 .

## Can You Paint Aluminum Siding?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/can-you-paint-aluminum-siding/
Updated: 2025-10-24
Summary: Yes, you can paint aluminum siding. It offers multiple benefits such as improved appearance, extended lifespan, increased property value, and much more.

Can You Paint Aluminum Siding?
Jun 30, 2025
Aluminum siding is a popular option for homeowners because of its durable and long-lasting nature. But over time, it can start to look dull, faded, or worn out. A common question people ask is whether you can paint aluminum siding. The good news is, yes, you can!
Painting aluminum siding is a low-cost option to give your home’s exterior a new and refreshed look!
Why Paint Aluminum Siding?
Painting aluminum siding is a budget-friendly way to refresh your home’s look without needing to replace the siding. Here are some reasons why painting is a great idea:
Improves Appearance
Over time, the siding can fade , look chalky, or become outdated. A fresh coat of paint instantly makes your home look clean, bright, and modern.
Protects the Siding
Paint adds a protective layer that helps shield the siding from sun damage, rain, and other weather conditions, preventing further wear and tear.
Extends Lifespan
Instead of replacing your siding early, painting can help it last several more years, saving you money in the long run.
Increases Property Value
A well-maintained and freshly painted exterior boosts property value. If you are looking to sell your house, this could be a great way to attract potential buyers.
Gives You More Color Options
If you are tired of looking at the same home exterior for years, painting gives you an opportunity to change its look. With multiple colors and finishes, you can choose your preferred option.
Eco-Friendly Option
An old siding, if replaced, ends up in a landfill. This creates more waste. Painting your existing siding is a greener and environmentally sustainable choice.
Process of Painting Aluminum Siding
Every siding material has different painting protocols. Here is how professionals can help you paint aluminum siding:
Siding experts will inspect the siding for any cracks, dents, and damage. Before proceeding to painting, repairs must be made.
The siding is then washed and scrubbed to remove dust and debris.
The siding is sanded for smooth paint application and left to dry.
Then, professionals apply a bonding primer to help the paint grip better.
Professionals choose high-quality paints to give you the best results. The first and second coat of paint is applied.
Finally, the paint is left to dry.
How To Maintain A Painted Aluminum Siding
Aluminum siding requires minimal upkeep, and a paint coat does not change that. All you are required to do is hire professional siding cleaning services to maintain its look over the years.
Professional siding experts can safely remove dirt, grime, mold, and mildew without damaging the paint. They use the right tools and gentle cleaning solutions to keep the surface looking fresh and vibrant.
Regular professional cleaning also helps prevent buildup that could cause the paint to wear down over time, extending the life of your fence’s finish.
Overall Insight
Yes, you can paint aluminum siding. It not only improves siding appearance but also protects it, increases home value, extends its lifespan, and is also environmentally sustainable. You can choose from a variety of colors and finish options to match your home’s style.

## Can You Paint Vinyl Siding?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/can-you-paint-vinyl-siding/
Updated: 2026-03-16
Summary: Read this blog to learn if vinyl siding can be painted, how to choose the right paint, its pros and cons. Find out if it is really worth the money.

Can You Paint Vinyl Siding?
Dec 15, 2025
Yes, vinyl siding can be painted to refresh your home’s exterior. Painting is a budget-friendly option compared to replacing siding, but it only works well when the siding is in good condition. Cracked, warped, or very old panels should be replaced before considering paint. Otherwise, you might lose money on the painting project, too.
Read this blog to find out the pros and cons of painting vinyl siding, and whether it is really worth it!
Why Homeowners Choose to Paint Vinyl Siding
Over time, vinyl can fade due to sun exposure, making a home look worn out. Painting restores color and improves appearance but does not add the same long-term protection as factory-finished vinyl. Homeowners may opt for it to forego the high cost of replacing the entire siding.
Some modern paints are designed to reduce heat buildup on vinyl. This prevents peeling and cracking of paint and helps your painted vinyl siding last longer.
How to Choose the Best Paint for Vinyl Siding
Choosing the right paint is essential. Vinyl siding requires 100% acrylic latex paint made specifically for vinyl surfaces. These paints are designed to stick properly and last longer outdoors. You can go for well-known brands to ensure that they are authentic and provide the best value for money.
Apart from paint type, color choice is also important. Lighter colors or shades similar to the original color are recommended. Dark colors absorb more heat, which can cause vinyl to warp or bend easily. You can ask professionals based on your existing siding color and preferences.
Weather and Timing Considerations
Weather plays a big role in how long painted vinyl siding lasts. Mild, dry conditions are best for painting. Extremely hot, cold, windy, or humid weather can affect how paint dries and sticks to the surface. So, it is always best to schedule the services in the best weather for vinyl painting.
How Long Does Painted Vinyl Siding Last
Painted vinyl siding can look good for several years when done correctly, though lifespan varies based on climate and sun exposure. In order to improve its overall longevity, regular inspections are important.
Pros of Painting Vinyl Siding
Costs less than replacing siding
Improves curb appeal quickly
Extends the life of existing siding
Offers a color update without a major renovation
Cons of Painting Vinyl Siding
Limited to lighter color choices
Requires proper preparation
Will not fix damaged or failing siding
Poor application can lead to peeling
Is Painting Vinyl Siding Worth It?
Painting vinyl siding is a smart option for homeowners who want an affordable exterior update. As long as the siding is in good shape and the right materials are used, painting vinyl siding can deliver long-lasting results, making it worth it for all the right reasons!
Overall Insight
Painting vinyl siding is a cost-effective home improvement project. But it is important to make sure that the existing siding is in good condition. Otherwise, it can lead to peeling paint and cracking. It is recommended to choose light colors or those that match the existing shade for best results.
If you are also looking to refresh your home’s exterior on a budget, get personalized advice from siding experts at Everest Siding and Windows . Call us at (832) 334-2528 to book a site visit.

## Caring For Your LP SmartSide Siding
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/caring-for-your-lp-smartside-siding/
Updated: 2024-01-30
Summary: The professional consultants at Everest Siding And Windows are knowledgeable and equipped to assist you

Caring For Your LP SmartSide Siding
Aug 26, 2019
The professional consultants at Everest Siding And Windows are knowledgeable and equipped to assist you in deciding which products are best for your home. Your roof and siding are crucial parts of the foundation of your home. Proper roofing and siding maintenance add to the aesthetic beauty and value of your home. For your convenience, we offer a no obligation, on-site consultation for all projects. We offer the highest quality products on the market at very competitive prices. Finance options are also available for all your home improvement projects. To find out more about how you can save money on your energy bills with our products, contact us today!
How Do You Care For SmartSide Siding?
If you want to increase the longevity of your LP SmartSide Siding , it is important that each year you take the time to visually inspect your homes exterior to assess any wear and tear your siding may have endured over the past year. Like all things, siding will need periodic maintenance performed to keep it functional and aesthetically pleasing.
Below are some tips for helping you get the most out of your LP SmartSide Siding.
Keep your siding clean and clear of dust and dirt build up. Wash the surface with a mild soap or white vinegar/ water mixture (1 part white vinegar and 3 parts water) and rinse well
Refrain from using a pressure washer as the high-pressure washing will cause moisture intrusion as well as likely damage the paint and cause discoloration
Avoid using harsh chemicals as this will damage your siding
Touch up chips and small imperfections using a cotton swab to apply matching paint to the bare areas. Avoid over-applying paint or trying to spread it out.
Make sure that your siding isn’t coming in constant contact with water. Some examples would be broken gutters that allow water to trickle down siding or sprinkler systems that are too close to your home
If you discover caulking around the siding that has cracked or lost its seal, hire a professional contractor to fix the problem
Hiring a professional will ensure that your siding repairs are effective. Everest Siding And Windows specializes in LP SmartSide Siding. This is a green-friendly engineered wood siding alternative to cement fiber siding that offers enhanced curb appeal to your home. For fast, efficient siding installation services, contact Everest Siding and Windows today.

## Caring for Your Vinyl Windows
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/caring-for-your-vinyl-windows/
Updated: 2024-01-30
Summary: Everest Siding And Windows is proud to sell vinyl windows that are energy efficient, cost-effective, and virtually maintenance free.

Caring for Your Vinyl Windows
Aug 26, 2019
Keep Them Clean & Clear!
Everest Siding And Windows is proud to sell vinyl windows that are energy efficient, cost-effective, and virtually maintenance free. However, while these windows are very easy to care for, routine cleaning is very necessary. Using products that will remove any mildew and grime from your interior and exterior vinyl windows will not only help your windows look clear and brand new, but it will also extend the life of your investment!
To preserve your vinyl windows, follow these cleaning tips a few times every year.
Cleaning Supplies You’ll Need!
There are many ways you can clean vinyl windows without damaging the surface. If you are just trying to get dust and dirt off, just mix together mild dish detergent and water. You will only have to use a small amount to clean the windows, and this way you won’t have to deal with any residue after rinsing. Use a paper towel to vigorously wipe any stains away; then rinse away the residue.
For tougher stains like grease, mildew, crayons or paint, you can trust a water-based household cleaner or a solution of 30% vinegar and 70% water. Instead of using a paper towel, use a soft, nonabrasive cloth.
What Products You Should Not Be Using
To maintain your vinyl windows, it’s important to not use aggressive organic solvents. Why? These substances could affect the surface appearance of the vinyl. Here are a few other cleansers to steer clear from nail polish remover, chlorine bleach, and liquid grease remover.
If you have any questions about maintaining your vinyl windows, don’t hesitate to reach out to us. We would be happy to talk to you.

## Common Window Installation Mistakes That Can Lead to Water Damage
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/common-window-installation-mistakes-that-can-lead-to-water-damage/
Updated: 2026-07-25
Summary: Is your window installation causing water leaks and rot? Learn how proper flashing and professional sealing protect your home from costly damage.

Common Window Installation Mistakes That Can Lead to Water Damage
Jul 15, 2026
Improper window installation is a frequent cause of residential water damage. When the seal around the frame fails, water leaks into the wall cavity. Over time, this leads to rot and mold. Ignoring these gaps might seem harmless, but water will eventually find a way inside.
Many homeowners rely on a bead of caulk for protection, but that is rarely the solution. Proper flashing is the primary requirement for keeping a home dry. If installers skip flashing or place it incorrectly, water pools behind the siding, which slowly destroys the wood framing of your home.
Improper Flashing Can Let Water Into Your Walls
Installers must make sure the sill pan flashing tilts toward the outside. It should also be tucked under the building paper. If the layers are out of order, water can easily get inside the wall. This causes hidden damage to your home’s wood frame.
If the flashing isn’t installed over the siding properly, water will drip behind the wall. A skilled installer layers these materials so that gravity pulls moisture away from the building rather than into it. Proper layering is the only way to keep the wall cavity dry.
Poor Sealing Leaves Windows Vulnerable to Leaks
Every joint needs high-quality sealant during window installation . Using the wrong product or a messy application causes early seal failure. Cracks grow as the house shifts over time. This leaves your home open to leaks during rain. Always use materials rated for your local climate.
The method of application matters as much as the product. A bad bead of caulk leaves tiny gaps. Air and water get through these spots easily. A smooth, steady seal keeps the window airtight. This protects your home when temperatures change or heavy storms hit.
Blocked Drainage Gaps Can Trap Moisture
Modern windows rely on weep holes to drain moisture away from the frame. If an installer happens to block these with too much sealant, water sits inside the unit and causes the sill to rot. You should inspect these channels regularly to ensure they stay open.
Many homeowners overlook these gaps, but they are the only way for water to drain if it gets past your exterior seals. Clearing out dirt and paint buildup is a simple, effective step to keep your windows in good shape for the long run.
Improper Window Leveling Creates Gaps for Water Intrusion
If a window is not installed level, it will not close tightly. This creates gaps that let in both air and water. Water can blow right through these spaces during a storm. Making sure the unit is square from the start prevents these leaks from developing later on.
A slight tilt might seem invisible to the naked eye, but the mechanical strain is immediate. When the window does not sit flush against the weatherstripping, the internal hardware also takes more pressure. This leads to harder operation and hardware failure long before the window reaches its expected lifespan.
In Summary
Quality installation is how you avoid expensive water damage. Getting the flashing and the frame sealed tight is what keeps moisture out of your walls for good. If your windows are leaking or you’re worried about future repairs, don’t wait for it to get worse. Get a professional to take a look. Call Everest Siding and Windows at (832) 334-2528 for an assessment.

## Dangers of the Lowest Bid
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/dangers-of-the-lowest-bid/
Updated: 2024-01-30
Summary: Contractors with integrity give you detailed and specific proposal the first time and include precise details of all materials and work needed.

Dangers of the Lowest Bid
Aug 26, 2019
Some contractors will simply throw out a low bid as a negotiating strategy.
Contractors with integrity give you detailed and specific proposal the first time and include precise details of all materials and work needed. If you are issued a bid without an explanation or on-site consultation, you should not only question it but the skill and professionalism of your contractor as well. It is just as important, to make a note of what is not detailed as well as what is included.
Every contractor is in business to make money.
If you receive a contractor bid that is 10% or more below other bids – it simply isn’t the same job. Quality companies will, for the most part, agree on the best way to complete a job. If their prediction varies greatly, they may be cutting corners or making a mistake.
If a bid seems to be good to be true, it is.
As noted in the quote from the Wall Street Journal above, it is easy to be fooled by the low quote and a “nice person”, but this isn’t usually the case. Call at least 3 references and ask about the end of the job cost versus the proposal.
Many contractors hide behind low prices.
Often times, the low bidder isn’t certified or using skilled labor and they are hoping if they offer a low price, you will overlook other shortcomings. An unlicensed contractor cheats the government and if they will do that they will just as likely cheat you. Avoiding them is a smart move.
Key Takeaways
There have been countless local and national news stories about unscrupulous contractors disappearing with homeowner deposits, operating without a license, or never completing their work and in most situations, the victims were blinded by a low-bid.
If you are seriously considering hiring any contractor with a very attractive bid to complete your commercial or residential remodeling project, make sure to do your research beforehand. Ask questions and get all of the answers in writing. A little legwork before you sign the contract could save you a great deal of time and effort down the line.
Everest Siding and Windows is a highly respected contractor in Houston Texas with multiple awards and strong customer guarantees. With over 20 years of residential and commercial remodeling experience, we are proud of the trusting relationships we build with each of our clients, crews, and suppliers. We offer no high pressure free in-home consultations and our proposal stands good for 12 months from the date of free consultation.
Warren Buffett: “Price Is What You Pay, Value Is What You Get”
“The Bitterness of Poor Quality Remains Long After the Sweetness of Low Price is Forgotten”
John Ruskin – “There is hardly anything in the world that someone cannot make a little worse and sell a little cheaper, and the people who consider price alone are that person’s lawful prey. It’s unwise to pay too much, but it’s worse to pay too little. When you pay too much, you lose a little money — that is all. When you pay too little, you sometimes lose everything, because the thing you bought was incapable of doing the thing it was bought to do. The common law of business balance prohibits paying a little and getting a lot — it can’t be done. If you deal with the lowest bidder, it is well to add something for the risk you run, and if you do that you will have enough to pay for something better.”

## Does Attic Ventilation Affect How Well a Radiant Barrier Works?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/does-attic-ventilation-affect-how-well-a-radiant-barrier-works/
Updated: 2026-09-08
Summary: Poor attic airflow can affect more than you think. Find out how ventilation and a radiant barrier work together to manage attic heat

Does Attic Ventilation Affect How Well a Radiant Barrier Works?
Aug 30, 2026
A radiant barrier and attic ventilation serve different purposes. One reflects radiant heat. The other removes hot air from the attic space. Because both operate within the same enclosed area, conditions created by one can influence how effectively the other performs.
What Does Attic Ventilation Do?
Attic ventilation’s main function is to remove hot air before it accumulates. It also helps manage moisture levels and maintains consistent airflow through the space. Ventilation, however, is not insulation and not a radiant barrier. It functions more like a release valve, allowing heat to escape rather than accumulate.
How Does a Radiant Barrier Manage Attic Heat?
A radiant barrier operates differently than insulation, despite the two often being discussed together. Insulation slows the transfer of heat. A radiant barrier reflects radiant heat before it can be absorbed by attic surfaces. When less heat is absorbed at the roof deck, less heat typically transfers down into the living space below.
A roof radiant barrier installation generally performs best as part of a larger system, one where the attic already has adequate ventilation and sufficient insulation in place. On its own, without those supporting elements, its effectiveness is more limited.
What Happens When an Attic Has Poor Ventilation?
When airflow is restricted, hot air remains trapped longer than it should. Heat builds, and moisture becomes harder to manage as a result. None of that means the radiant barrier stops functioning. It continues reflecting radiant heat regardless of how stale the surrounding air becomes. What actually changes is the condition of the attic itself. Poor airflow and higher heat retention create a more challenging environment, regardless of what else is installed in the attic.
Can Ventilation and a Radiant Barrier Work Together?
A well-functioning attic does not depend on a single product to perform all the work. It typically relies on three separate systems working together. The following outlines how each one contributes:
A radiant barrier reflects radiant heat.
Ventilation removes hot air and maintains airflow.
Insulation slows heat transfer between the attic and the living space.
None of these can substitute for the other two. Skip the insulation, and a radiant barrier provides only limited benefit. Without adequate ventilation, heat continues to build even when insulation is in place. The best-performing attics usually have all three working together.
What Should Houston Homeowners Consider?
Houston’s summer heat is prolonged, typically extending from May through September, and attics absorb much of that heat. During hot weather, roof surfaces and attic spaces can become significantly warmer than the conditioned living space below. Before installing a radiant barrier, it is worth evaluating what is already in place. Is the ventilation performing adequately? What condition is the insulation in? How are the roof and attic actually laid out? In some cases, a full attic efficiency evaluation is a better approach than a single fix.
When Should You Have Your Attic Evaluated?
A few signs point to needing an attic evaluation. Upstairs rooms running noticeably hotter than the rest of the house is one. So is an attic that feels excessively hot, or cooling costs that remain high even when the HVAC system is functioning properly. These issues typically point back to insulation or ventilation falling short, rather than the radiant barrier being an incorrect choice.
Conclusion
Attic ventilation does affect the environment in which a radiant barrier operates, even though the two serve separate functions. An attic that has been properly evaluated often benefits from a combination of ventilation, insulation, and radiant heat control working together, rather than relying on a single component.
Everest Siding and Windows can help homeowners evaluate attic conditions and determine whether a radiant barrier is appropriate for their home. Call (832) 334-2528 to learn more.

## Energy Efficiency & Staying Cool in the Summer
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/energy-efficiency-staying-cool-in-the-summer/
Updated: 2024-12-24
Summary: Discover practical energy-saving tips to beat the heat this summer, keep your home cool, and reduce electricity bills effortlessly!

Energy Efficiency & Staying Cool in the Summer
Aug 26, 2019
Learn How You Can Stay Cool for Less This Summer
Energy-efficient products are key to staying cool in the summertime at lower costs! When it’s hot outside, it helps to have features you can count on to keep your cooling costs low and your indoor comfort at an all-time high.
Energy efficiency starts from the outside! Learn how these products can improve your indoor comfort this summer.
Siding:
Instead of using the popular Tyvek house wrap which only helps keep air and water out, use the Low-E house wrap which also provides an R-value of 5. The R-value refers to an insulating material’s resistance to conductive heat flow and how it is measured or rated in terms of its thermal resistance. The higher the R-value, the greater the insulating effectiveness. With this type of insulation, your home’s interior can better maintain interior temperatures, which will reduce the amount of energy your air conditioner uses. Two good options for your home are LP SmartSide and HardiePlank siding .
Windows:
With energy-efficient vinyl windows you can enjoy lower HVAC costs, improved comfort, reduced condensation, reduced unwanted heat gain, increased light, and reduced fading to your carpeting and furniture. You will see and feel the difference your energy-efficient windows will have in your home right away!
Roofs:
Also known as cool roofs, energy efficient roofs made out of materials such as metal, asphalt, clay or concrete tile, slate, wood shake or laminate are beneficial for any home in the Texas area. We choose these materials for roof replacements because of their many cooling advantages in the summertime! Rather than heat being absorbed into the roof, traveling down into your home, a correctly installed, roof, will significantly reduce the heat passing through. Boasting emittance and reflectance abilities, energy efficient roofs won’t absorb the heat from the sun’s UV rays. In fact, reflectance will reflect the sun’s energy back into the atmosphere, keeping your home nice and cool! A great and affordable option for increasing energy efficiency is to add one or two solar fans to your roof. Solar Fans run on solar power and pull super-heated air out of your attic to be replaced by cooler outside air. This reduces the amount of work your HVAC system has to do to cool your upstairs living area.
Schedule Your Free Consultation Today!
If you’d like to learn more about these energy efficient products, or you’d like to invest in them today, call Everest Siding And Windows. We proudly serve clients in Houston, Cypress, Spring, The Woodlands, Katy, TX and the surrounding communities. We look forward to making your home cooler this summer and helping you save on your energy bills! Contact us today to set up an on-site consultation to receive your no obligation estimate.

## How Does Houston Weather Affect HardiePlank Siding?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/how-does-houston-weather-affect-hardieplank-siding/
Updated: 2026-08-20
Summary: See how Houston's heat, storms, and humidity impact HardiePlank siding, and what homeowners should watch for to avoid damage.

How Does Houston Weather Affect HardiePlank Siding?
Aug 15, 2026
Houston’s weather can be demanding, particularly during the hot and humid months. Between the heat, the humidity, and the storms that roll through several months a year, a home’s exterior faces conditions most siding materials were never designed for. HardiePlank holds up better than many alternatives, but understanding how the local climate interacts with it helps homeowners get more out of the material over time.
Houston Heat and HardiePlank Siding
Summers here bring intense heat, direct sun, and high humidity, and that kind of prolonged exposure causes some materials to warp or crack. Fiber cement does not share that weakness in the same way. HardiePlank is engineered to resist heat-related expansion and contraction. When installed correctly, it tends to hold its shape and color longer than many vinyl or wood products exposed to the same sun.
Humidity and Moisture Exposure
Gulf Coast humidity lingers in the air for most of the year, and that constant moisture is where many siding problems begin. HardiePlank generally resists rot and swelling better than wood, though it is not immune to the effects of poor installation. Gaps, unsealed joints, or improperly caulked seams can let moisture behind the boards.
Once that happens, the greater risk often lies with the structure underneath rather than the siding material itself. Working with an experienced Hardie Plank Siding Contractor for routine sealing and upkeep helps close off that entry point before it becomes a larger issue.
Heavy Rain and Storm Conditions
Houston experiences its share of downpours, tropical storms, and occasional hurricane threats, all of which can put exterior siding through demanding conditions. HardiePlank is designed to withstand heavy rain and wind-driven debris reasonably well, though repeated storm exposure still takes a toll over the years. Cracked boards, loosened panels, or small chips from flying debris are not always visible from the ground. A quick walk around the exterior after a severe storm season can catch damage before it worsens.
Maintaining HardiePlank Through Houston’s Weather
An inspection twice a year catches most problems while they are still minor. Homeowners should look for cracking, chipping, or areas where paint has started to peel, and keep the surface clear of dirt, mildew, and debris, particularly in shaded or damp corners of the house. Addressing damage before the next rainy stretch is generally easier than waiting until it spreads further.
Why Proper Installation Matters in Houston
Even high-quality siding performs only as well as its installation. Improper nailing, poor flashing, or gaps at the seams can undermine what HardiePlank is designed to do, especially in a climate that shifts between extreme heat and heavy rain within the same week. Working with an installer experienced in Houston’s specific conditions makes a measurable difference in how the siding performs over time.
Protecting Your Home Through Every Season
Houston’s weather rarely lets up, and durable siding paired with routine maintenance plays a major role in protecting a home through every season. Reach out to Everest Siding & Windows at (832) 334-2528 to learn more about HardiePlank siding and professional installation options for your Houston home.

## How Does Roof Insulation Impact Energy Bills?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/how-does-roof-insulation-impact-energy-bills/
Updated: 2026-10-28
Summary: Learn how roof insulation lowers energy bills by reducing heat loss and gain, improving comfort, and boosting efficiency in every season.

How Does Roof Insulation Impact Energy Bills?
Feb 28, 2026
Energy costs are climbing higher every year, leaving most homeowners hunting for any way to trim their monthly overhead. One of the most effective fixes is also one of the most overlooked: proper roof insulation.
Your roof acts as a thermal bridge, letting heat flow in and out of your home. Once you grasp how insulation acts as a barrier, you can start seeing real savings on your utility bills while finally staying comfortable year-round.
What Is Roof Insulation, and Why Is It Important?
Think of roof insulation as a thermal blanket for your home. Its job is to slow down the movement of heat. In the dead of winter, it keeps that expensive warm air from escaping, and in the summer, it stops the sun’s baking heat from turning your living room into an oven.
Without enough insulation, your AC and heater have to run a marathon just to maintain a decent temperature. That extra strain doesn’t just make your house uncomfortable; it shows up directly on your monthly bill as wasted energy. Proper insulation plugs those leaks and makes your entire home more efficient.
How Roof Insulation Reduces Heating Costs
We all know that heat rises. In a poorly insulated house, that warm air you’re paying for heads straight for the attic and disappears through the roof. This forces your furnace or boiler to work double-time to replace what’s being lost.
Good insulation traps that heat where it belongs. By stabilizing the indoor temperature, your heating system can take a breather. Over the long haul, this saves you a massive amount of money and actually extends the lifespan of your HVAC equipment since it isn’t running 24/7.
How Insulating Your Roof Can Save You Money on Cooling Costs
In summer, the sun heats your shingles until your roof temperature rises significantly. Without a solid barrier, that heat radiates straight down into your living space.
Adding high-quality insulation keeps that outdoor heat where it stays—outside. You can stay cool without redlining your AC unit. When the demand on your cooling system drops, your electricity usage drops right along with it, giving you a much more manageable summer budget.
Using Less Energy Makes You More Comfortable
Beyond the money, insulation is about how your home feels. It gets rid of those annoying hot and cold spots, keeping the temperature steady from room to room. You won’t have to constantly fiddle with the thermostat just to feel okay.
When your home naturally holds its temperature, you simply don’t need to lean on your HVAC system as much. This isn’t just great for your wallet; it’s also a big win for the environment since you’re lowering your overall carbon footprint.
The Role of Insulation Materials and Installation
Not all insulation is created equal. Whether you go with fiberglass, spray foam, cellulose, or rigid boards, the “R-value” is what matters. That number tells you how well the material resists heat flow.
However, even the best material won’t do much if it’s installed poorly. Professional installation ensures there are no gaps or compressed spots that let air bypass the barrier. If you want to see the biggest drop in your energy bills, you need the right material paired with a flawless installation.
Long-Term Financial Benefits of Roof Insulation
Yes, there is an upfront cost to insulating a roof, but it’s an investment that actually pays you back. Between the lower monthly bills and the reduced need for HVAC repairs, most homeowners see a full return on their investment within just a few years.
Plus, a well-insulated home is a huge selling point. Modern buyers are looking for energy-efficient features, so upgrading your insulation can actually bump up your property value when it’s time to head to market.
How to Tell if Your Roof Insulation Needs Better Insulation
If your energy bills are creeping up or your upstairs is ten degrees hotter than your downstairs, your insulation is likely failing you. Other warning signs include ice dams on the gutters in winter or an AC unit that never seems to turn off.
A professional energy audit can pinpoint exactly where your insulation is thin and show you where you’re losing money every single day.
In Conclusion
Your roof insulation dictates the climate of your home more than almost any other factor. If some rooms feel like a sauna while others feel like a fridge, your insulation isn’t doing its job.
The team at Everest Siding and Windows is here to help you lock in your comfort and lower those bills. Reach out to us at (832) 334 2528 to get your home insulated the right way.

## How Does Siding Impact Commercial Property Value?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/how-does-siding-impact-commercial-property-value/
Updated: 2024-08-08
Summary: Siding might not seem important, but it frames your house and adds to the aesthetic value, impacting the commercial property value too.

How Does Siding Impact Commercial Property Value?
Jan 30, 2024
Siding is often regarded as the aesthetic covering of one’s house, but despite its outward appearance, there are a lot of uses it offers. Even though it is usually overlooked, siding plays a huge role in shaping the overall value of commercial properties. Besides its aesthetic appeal, siding also acts as a protective shield, battling off external stimuli and other elements that can significantly impact a property’s worth. However, if you want to know how exactly siding impacts commercial property value, make sure to keep reading this blog.
Does Siding Impact Property Value?
Believe it or not, yes. The exterior of any type of commercial property serves as its first impression, and just like people say, the first impression is the last impression. Plus, when it comes to visual factors, it is necessary to catch the customer’s attention the moment they lay their eyes on the property.
Potential buyers are more likely to be attracted to a property with well-maintained siding. This is because siding not only enhances the curb appeal but also conveys a sense of professionalism and elegance. However, a neglected or worn-out exterior can decrease the value of the property, causing the buyers to turn away.
Not many homeowners realize this, but siding can make or break a commercial property’s worth. Take a look below to see all the different ways it impacts the overall property value.
It Adds to The Curb Appeal
The external appearance of a commercial property sets the tone for what lies on the inside. Not to mention, an aesthetically appealing exterior can give way to increased foot traffic, which in turn leads to a higher property value.
Protects Property From Outside Elements
Siding acts as a shield, protecting the house from harsh weather conditions such as rain, wind, snow, storms, etc. However, well-insulated and weather-resistant siding makes sure that the property lasts longer, with low maintenance costs. The durability and reliability are what ultimately increase the property’s value.
Offers Energy Efficiency
If you want to step it up, you can always opt for siding materials that are environmentally friendly and energy-efficient. Plus, most buyers these days look for sustainable options that enhance insulation and cut back on utility costs.
Doesn’t Cost a Lot in Maintenance
Investing in high-quality siding that requires minimal maintenance is a great strategy since it reduces the overall costs and instead adds to the appearance. Most buyers look for low-maintenance options, which could work in your favor.
Easy to Customize
One of the best things about siding is that it is customizable. You can add to the design or change it according to your preferences. This helps homeowners upgrade to the latest trends, giving the exterior of their homes a makeover without spending too much money.
Bottom Line
In short, siding tends to significantly impact a commercial property’s value. However, it is ultimately up to you and how you design the siding, as the end costs depend entirely on the functionality and aesthetic appeal of the siding. Nevertheless, for quick maintenance tips and siding repair, give our experts at Everest Siding and Windows a call at (832) 334-2528 .

## How Long Do Double Pane Windows Last
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/how-long-do-double-pane-windows-last/
Updated: 2024-08-08
Summary: The average lifespan of double pane windows is around 15-20 years. Learn about the signs when you should replace it.

How Long Do Double Pane Windows Last
Jun 30, 2024
Just like everything at our house, double pane windows also have a definite lifespan. Although high quality windows can qualify to stand the test of time, it is important to keep in mind that nothing lasts forever.
So, the question we are dealing with here is, how long do double pane windows last? The typical lifespan of a double pan window ranges between 15-20 years, keeping guarantees aside. The varying of years is highly tentative depending on the type and quality of material used, professional installation and the location of windows.
How Often Should We Replace Windows?
Windows are meant to stand the test of time. Which is why, there are very few times we see or hear that a window is being repaired or replaced unless it is a full-fledged renovation or serious damage. However, it is not a foolproof scenario – the lifespan of windows can greatly vary depending on the location, material, quality of installation and much more.
Sins You Should Replace Your Double Pane Window
Leaving window replacements’ for long can affect the safety and energy efficiency of your home. This is why it is important to know the signs of malfunction.
Condensation Build-Up
One of the biggest warning signs of a failing seal is seeing fog or condensation build-up between the window layers, this is a sign that outdoor air is getting inside. This temperature difference can lead to visible buildup of moisture. apart from being plainly unsightly, it is important to note that your windows are no longer serving any purpose.
Outdoor Noises
A double pan window is designed to block outdoor noises. If you find that you are hearing more noises than usual, this could be a sign that your window seal is breaking.
Rising Heat and Cooling Cost
The primary sign of a faulty window is lower energy efficiency. You can notice a high electricity or gas bill and a risen indoor temperature. If you are suspecting the hike in your energy cost, it could possibly be because of a faulty window.
Sudden Air Drafts
A poor seal around your window panes can allow air to come inside. The best way to diagnose this is you run your finger around the perimeter of the frame to see if you feel any air. If yes, professional inspection can provide detailed answers if the air is coming through a replaceable weatherstripping or broken seal.
Visible Damage
Panes can sometimes collapse and cause visible damage. You can talk to a professional window replacement service to get prompt resolutions of replacing glass, wooden frames or any other component.
Falling of Decorative Grid
Dual paned windows have a decorative grid between the layers. The materials holding this grid in place can lose their integrity over time. When this happens,the grid lines tend to fall out of their desired place. In most cases, replacement is recommended to restore the look of your windows!
Final Words
Double pane windows provide great functional use in homes. They offer insulation, better energy efficiency, and privacy in homes. However, they are suspected of physical damage.
If you are also suspecting issues with your double pane window, contact experts at Everest Siding and Windows for inspection and quality service. Call us at (832) 334-2528 .

## How Long Does Antimicrobial Coating Last on Exterior Surfaces?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/how-long-does-antimicrobial-coating-last-on-exterior-surfaces/
Updated: 2026-07-08
Summary: Outdoor coatings kill germs and stop paint decay. Learn how long these protective treatments stay active on your exterior walls.

How Long Does Antimicrobial Coating Last on Exterior Surfaces?
Jun 30, 2026
Outdoor walls and pipes constantly gather mold, algae, and dark grime. Standard pressure washing removes this dirt but does not stop new germs from growing back immediately. This guide breaks down how long different exterior protective treatments actually last.
How Long Do Spray-On Exterior Treatments Last?
Spray-applied antimicrobial treatments can remain effective for several weeks or months, depending on the product and environmental conditions. These liquids form a thin shield against green mold. However, direct sunlight and heavy rain can gradually reduce the coating’s effectiveness over time.
Public benches or metal rails lose defense quicker. People touch these items all day. Frequent contact and abrasion can wear down some antimicrobial treatments more quickly, making periodic reapplication necessary.
Can Built-In Surface Protection Last For Years?
Germ protection can be built directly into hardware. Manufacturers mix it into light fixtures and exterior pipes during production. This defense generally lasts as long as the product is usable.
This method mixes copper or silver ions straight into raw parts. The protection exists throughout the whole object. Rain cannot wash it away. You get daily defense without monthly maintenance work.
What Weather Issues Hurt Outdoor Surface Defenses?
Local weather directly affects how well a treatment performs. Environmental conditions such as temperature and moisture can influence how effectively some antimicrobial coatings perform. In dry, freezing winter conditions, these same treatments show a major drop in performance.
Debris also lowers effectiveness. If thick mud, dust, or dead leaves cover the treated surface, the active layer cannot touch new microbes. Regular pressure washing is still necessary to keep the antimicrobial coating clear and working.
How Do Chemical and Mechanical Products Kill Microbes?
Chemical antimicrobial treatments use ingredients such as silver or copper ions to disrupt microbial cell functions and reduce the growth of certain microorganisms. Their effectiveness and contact time vary depending on the product and environmental conditions.
Mechanical options use physical force. The coating dries into millions of tiny microscopic spikes. These sharp spikes pop the cell walls immediately on contact. Germs cannot build up any resistance to physical contact.
How Does Proper Maintenance Extend Coating Lifespan?
Heavy dirt blocks new germs from making direct contact with the active ingredients. Mud and tree sap coat the surface completely. When that happens, the treatment stops working. You need to rinse away this debris so the surface can kill germs again.
Do not use harsh chemicals or power washers on these treated walls. Hard scrubbing strips the protective layer straight off the surface. A simple garden hose and mild soap will clean the area without ruining the defense.
Final Thoughts
Weather and mold will ruin outdoor walls if they are left unprotected. A good exterior coating stops this damage before it starts, keeping your home clean without constant scrubbing. All you have to do is rinse the surface occasionally to keep the defense working for years.
If you want to shield your home from the elements, the team at Everest Siding And Windows can help. Call (832) 334-2528 today to find the right durable option for your property.

## How Long Does Hardieplank Last?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/how-long-does-hardieplank-last/
Updated: 2026-10-28
Summary: How long does Hardieplank last? It's as strong as a brick. With care, it can last for 30 years and even more. It's cement mixed with cellulose for strength.

How Long Does Hardieplank Last?
Mar 30, 2026
You know how technology keeps advancing, even in things like home siding? There’s Hardieplank siding made from fiber cement. Many people, about 5.5 million families, have switched to it because it’s super durable.
Some folks still like sticking with old favorites like wood or vinyl because if it worked for Grandpa, it should work for us. There’s nothing wrong with that, but how long does Hardieplank last? The answer seems promising.
What Is the Life Expectancy of HardiePlanks?
James Hardie is the top company for fiber cement siding in North America. They have been leading the way in quality siding for many years. Their siding can last a long time, even over 50 years.
They guarantee it for 30 years and the trim boards for 15 years, but it can last even longer with proper installation and care. But here’s the thing: you’ve got to pick the right contractor to install it properly in your house.
Deciding Factors for How Long Does Hardieplank Last
While Hardie’s fiber cement materials are tough and can withstand weather, if they are not put on your house correctly, they won’t hold up as long as they’re supposed to. The following are the factors that decide their durability:
Durable Material
James Hardie’s siding is made from fiber cement, which makes it strong and long-lasting. Unlike other types of siding, it won’t rot, warp, or crack easily. This durability is a big reason Hardie siding can last for many years.
Performance Additives
Hardie Siding has also added special stuff to make it even better. These additives make it fire-resistant, waterproof, and able to handle any kind of weather. So, right off the bat, it’s already tougher and lasts longer than other types of siding.
Proper Installation is Key
Putting up Hardie siding isn’t just about the material – it’s about how it’s installed. If it’s not put up correctly, it won’t look good or work like it should, which means it won’t last as long.
Following Best Practices
James Hardie gives instructions on properly installing their siding, and installers must follow these guidelines. If they don’t, the siding won’t perform as well as it should and won’t last as long.
Using the Right Materials
Installing Hardie siding means using the right materials, like the correct nails, caulk, and paint. If the wrong materials are used, like low-quality caulk or the wrong type of paint, the siding won’t hold up as well over time. So, using the right materials to ensure the siding lasts is crucial.
How to Ensure the Longevity of Hardie Planks?
Knowing that Hardie’s siding needs to be put up correctly and with the right stuff is key to understanding how long it will last on your house. You must find a reliable contractor who knows what they are doing to double-check that your Hardie siding sticks around for the long haul.
Doing your homework, asking the right questions, and knowing what to watch out for will help you find a top-notch contractor. Once you have the right one, you can feel good about investing in James Hardie siding that will keep your home looking great for years.
Final Word
And here you have it above: your detailed answer to “How long does Hardieplanks Last?” Are you Considering getting new siding for your home? Contact our certified installer, Richard, at Everest Siding & Windows .
Everyone working in our company is not only certified to install but has also been trained directly by the manufacturer. This includes everyone on the crew, from the leader to the rest of the team. Call us at (832) 334-2528 to book an appointment.
