## How to Spot and Prevent Wood Rot Behind Your Siding
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/how-to-spot-and-prevent-wood-rot-behind-your-siding/
Updated: 2025-11-18
Summary: Find out how to spot and prevent wood rot behind siding. Call professionals for inspection, repair, and replacement services.

How to Spot and Prevent Wood Rot Behind Your Siding
Oct 15, 2025
Wood rot behind siding is a common issue homeowners face. Not only can it affect the appearance of your siding, but it can also compromise your home’s structure. In this blog, we will talk about how to spot wood rot behind your siding and ways you can treat and prevent it.
So, if you happen to have wood siding in your home, this blog will be a helpful read!
Ways To Spot Wood Rot Behind Siding
Wood rot forms when moisture gets trapped behind the siding. Here is how you can spot it:
Check your siding at least twice a year, especially in spring and fall, for early signs of damage.
Dark or stained patches on wood often indicate moisture problems.
Gently press on the wood. If it feels soft or spongy, you might be dealing with rot.
Mold, mildew, or white and yellow patches can signal wood rot on your siding.
Check for splitting, bulging, or warped panels. This signals that moisture is trapped behind.
A damp or moldy smell near siding is a red flag.
Inspect near gutters, window trim, the bottom edges of siding, and around shrubs for trapped moisture.
Common Causes of Wood Rot Behind Siding
Wood rot develops when moisture seeps behind siding due to:
Leaky gutters or poor drainage
Inadequate ventilation
Damaged or unsealed siding
Overgrown plants trapping moisture
Debris or dirt build-up against the walls
Poorly maintained or unpainted wood
How to Prevent Wood Rot Behind Siding
The best way to prevent wood rot is to keep moisture out and ensure proper airflow. Here’s how:
Regular Maintenance
Inspect your siding twice a year and after heavy storms. Seal any cracks, holes, or gaps with high-quality exterior caulk. This prevents moisture and wood rot.
Ensure Proper Drainage
Keep gutters and downspouts clean and make sure they direct water away from the house.
Maintain Good Ventilation
Use soffit vents and ensure attic airflow to help moisture evaporate instead of getting trapped behind siding.
Seal and Protect
Repaint or restain wood siding every 5–7 years using weather-resistant coatings. Always prime bare wood before painting. Get personalized advice from professionals.
Trim Landscaping
Keep bushes, vines, and trees at least 12–36 inches away from siding to prevent moisture buildup.
Avoid Contact with Objects
Don’t lean ladders, firewood, or other materials against the siding. They trap moisture and contribute to wood rotting.
Use Treated or Rot-Resistant Wood
When replacing siding or trim, consider options that are treated and resistant to rot. While it may seem like a costly investment, these options offer better performance in the long run.
Keep It Clean
Regularly remove leaves, dirt, and debris from around siding and gutters to minimize moisture and chances of developing wood rot.
Final Word
Wood rot behind siding can occur due to trapped moisture caused by leaking gutters, inadequate ventilation, unsealed siding, overgrown plants, debris, and unsealed wood. You can spot it through damp spots, mold, gently pressing, and checking for warping, bulging, or splitting.
If you spot wood rot on your siding, schedule professional inspection services at Everest Siding and Windows . We will inspect, repair, or replace siding depending on the damage. Call us at (832) 334-2528 .

## Is Brick Waterproofing a Good Idea for Damaged Walls?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/is-brick-waterproofing-a-good-idea-for-damaged-walls/
Updated: 2026-10-28
Summary: Tired of having damaged walls because of water issues? Learn how brick waterproofing can help you prevent damage to your walls, like cracks or spalling.

Is Brick Waterproofing a Good Idea for Damaged Walls?
Jul 30, 2025
Using bricks is one of the oldest ways of building walls. Because of their durability and natural finish, they are popular all over the world. However, one of the downsides of using bricks is their ability to absorb water. This vulnerability can cause the bricks to rupture, ruining the aesthetics of the wall with constant leaks and cracks.
However, all of this can be avoided with brick waterproofing. With this process, you can enhance the lifespan of your wall structure. In this blog, we will explore how brick waterproofing can help you in dealing with damaged walls and how this process is carried out. So, let’s begin!
What Is Brick Waterproofing?
Brick waterproofing is a process that can help you preserve the natural structure and integrity of the bricks. By protecting the bricks from water infiltration, you can extend the lifespan of your property’s structure. Especially if you are living in areas with heavy rainfall and dampness, brick waterproofing can help you avoid mold and other damage caused by excessive water in the bricks.
How Is Brick Waterproofing Done?
Brick waterproofing is a time-consuming process. However, the results can help you maintain the integrity of the bricks used in building your property. Here is how brick waterproofing is done:
Preparation – The surface of the bricks is cleaned thoroughly to remove dust and dirt. After that, all the holes and cracks are filled to start the repair.
Sealants – Sealants made from silanes and siloxanes are applied to the bricks to create a barrier.
Coatings – A coating of waterproof paint is applied to the bricks.
Application – A coating of another sealant is applied using a brush or a roller.
How Does Waterproofing Bricks Help Damaged Walls?
If your walls have started showing signs of damage, then don’t think it is too late. You can still preserve the structure of your wall with brick waterproofing. Here is a breakdown of how this process helps already damaged walls:
Prevents Further Damage
A damaged wall can cause more leaks and structural damage. To prevent this, you need to consider brick waterproofing. Experts will fill in all the gaps and holes with sealants to make sure there is no further deterioration.
Stops Mold Growth
By blocking the moisture, the likelihood of mold and mildew growth becomes less. This also prevents any health hazards and stops the wall from further damage.
Thermal Efficiency
A wet brick will conduct heat less effectively. When the walls are dry, the heat is optimal. By waterproofing your bricks, you can enhance thermal efficiency in your home and reduce your energy bills.
Protection Against Freeze-Thaw
If you are living in areas with freezing temperatures, then water can freeze and expand inside the bricks. To prevent that, waterproofing the bricks is necessary.
Final Thoughts
To maintain a good structure of any property, it is important to take care of the walls. Having bricks as a part of the structure can add a natural aesthetic to the wall. However, they can absorb water quickly. Excessive absorption can cause the growth of mold, and it can also ruin the structure of the bricks by causing leaks and cracks. To avoid this, you need to get brick waterproofing done. This process can help you maintain the structure of your bricks.
To get reliable brick waterproofing services, you can always contact Everest Siding and Windows . We will make sure your investment in bricks stands the test of time. Call us now at (832) 334-2528 for a free consultation.

Summary: Discover why LP SmartSide siding is a top choice for Katy, Cypress, and Tomball homes with expert installation from Everest Siding and Windows.

Is LP SmartSide Worth It in Texas? Feedback From Katy, Cypress and Tomball Homeowners
Feb 4, 2026

Many homeowners in Katy, Cypress, and Tomball have turned to LP SmartSide siding for its combination of durability, appearance, and value. What is LP SmartSide Siding?
LP SmartSide is engineered wood siding designed to provide the look of traditional wood with greater strength and resistance to common problems like rotting, cracking, and insect damage. Unlike natural wood, LP SmartSide comes pretreated with a proprietary process that includes zinc borate for protection against fungi and termites. This makes it particularly suited for the humid and sometimes extreme weather conditions in Texas.
Benefits of LP SmartSide for Katy Homeowners
Homeowners in Katy have praised LP SmartSide for its long-lasting beauty and ease of maintenance. After replacing their old cedar siding, many families report that their home not only looks refreshed but is better protected against heavy rains and the Texas sun.

## Is Malarkey Roofing Worth The Cost?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/is-malarkey-roofing-worth-the-cost/
Updated: 2026-10-28
Summary: Malarkey Roofing is definitely worth the cost due to extreme durability, versatile options and certified installation.

Is Malarkey Roofing Worth The Cost?
Dec 30, 2024
A roof replacement is a heavy investment. Homeowners are looking for materials that serve a durable and aesthetic finish. In order to achieve this; we at Everest Siding and Windows recommend our clients Malarkey Roofing Products . These are pricey, but offer long term value to your property. In this blog, we will build more on this type of roofing material and how you can incorporate it in your home!
About Malarkey Roofing Products
Malarkey Roofing Products has been a leading name in the roofing industry since 1953. Based in Portland, Oregon, this family-owned company is known for its eco-friendly and durable roofing materials.
While Malarkey shingles can be pricey, their quality, longevity, and appearance have earned them high praise from homeowners and roofers.
Three Types of Malarkey Roofing Shingles
Malarkey offers three main types of shingles:
Architectural Shingles
Also called laminate shingles, these are the most popular. They come in four styles and offer features like solar reflectivity and high impact resistance.
Designer Shingles
These are larger, thicker, and more durable than architectural shingles. They feature dual-layer construction, enhancing weather resistance and curb appeal.
Three-Tab Shingles
Traditional and economical, these shingles are made with a single asphalt layer. They’re sturdy and offer reliable, long-term protection but lack the depth of the other styles.
Why Homeowners Love Malarkey Roofing Products
Here are some benefits of choosing Malarkey Roofing Products.
Versatile Options
These shingles come with various water barriers, underlayment, and ridge shingle options. For example, you can choose between affordable or high-performance underlayment options to suit your budget and needs.
Extreme Durability
These shingles withstand tough weather like wind, rain, hail, and snow. Malarkey Roofing Products have high impact ratings and wind warranties for up to 110 MPH. Their polymer-modified asphalt keeps them flexible and resistant to cracking as they age.
Eco-Friendly Design
Malarkey Roofing Products i.e, shingles mainly use upcycled rubber and plastic., extending their lifespan and reducing landfill waste. Special granules can convert smog into water-soluble ions, making your roof as environmentally impactful as planting two trees. Reflective granules are also available to improve energy efficiency in hot climates.
Stain Resistance
Special granules help prevent algae growth, keeping roofs clean and attractive in humid areas. Hence, reducing the chances of stains on your roof.
Certified Installation
Certified contractors are trained to install these products correctly, ensuring quality and reliability. Experts at Everest Siding can help you with your roof installation project.
A Few Drawbacks of Malarkey Roofing Products
The pros however outweigh the drawbacks of Malarkey Roofing Products, here are some points to make an informed choice!
High Cost
Malarkey shingles range from $73 to $170 per square. This price reflects their premium materials and quality installation, making them a worthwhile long-term investment.
Limited Styles
With only six styles available, Malarkey’s selection may seem limited. However, each style is thoroughly tested to ensure durability, performance, and curb appeal.
Are Malarkey Shingles Worth It?
Yes! Malarkey shingles are a smart investment. Their durability, eco-friendly design, and premium features outweigh the higher cost and limited options in design and styles.
Overall Insight
Roof replacements are a hefty investment. Which is why locals are looking for durable and long-lasting options. Among the unending list of roofing materials, nothing comes close to Malarkey Roofing Products. They are extremely durable, eco-friendly, and stain resistant. Everest Siding and Windows offers certified installation of Malarkey Roofing Products. Call us at (832) 334-2528 to get an estimate.

## Is Outdoor Kitchen Installation A Good Idea To Beat The Texan Summer?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/is-outdoor-kitchen-installation-a-good-idea-to-beat-the-texan-summer/
Updated: 2024-08-08
Summary: An outdoor kitchen installation is a worthy investment. It boosts home value, increases indoor space, keeps the house cool in summer, and appeals to buyers.

Is Outdoor Kitchen Installation A Good Idea To Beat The Texan Summer?
Mar 15, 2024
In Texas, cooking outside is deeply valued, especially BBQ. Instead of always going out to eat, why not become a BBQ expert yourself? With an outdoor kitchen, you can practice and cook for your friends and family right in your backyard.
Imagine having your cozy spot to hang out and cook! But before you can realize this dream, you must know how to plan your outdoor kitchen in Texas. Where do you begin, and what must you keep in mind?
Does Adding an Outdoor Kitchen Add Value?
Outdoor kitchens don’t just give you extra room to cook, eat, and have fun—they can also increase the financial value of your home. One big reason is that they increase the square footage of your living area.
What to Consider During Outdoor Kitchen Installation?
An outdoor kitchen should be a must-have accessory in your backyard, especially if you are a Texan resident, to keep the BBQ tradition strong for generations. The following are some crucial considerations:
Location: Choose a spot that is convenient for cooking and entertaining and has easy access to water and electricity.
Functionality: Consider what appliances and features you need, such as a grill, sink, refrigerator, and storage.
Durability: Opt for materials that can withstand outdoor conditions, such as stainless steel, stone, or weather-resistant wood.
Budget: Determine how much you’re willing to spend on the project, including materials, labor, and any additional features.
Design: Plan the layout and style of your outdoor kitchen to complement your home’s aesthetic and suit your cooking needs.
Maintenance: Consider the upkeep required for your outdoor kitchen, including cleaning, repairs, and protection from the elements.
Regulations: Check local building codes and zoning restrictions to ensure compliance with any regulations regarding outdoor kitchen installations.
Benefits of Installing an Outdoor Kitchen
An outdoor kitchen not only increases the resale value of your home. It changes your overall lifestyle for good. You can further:
Entertain Guests:
Your outdoor kitchen is perfect for having friends over. It becomes the place everyone wants to hang out, especially during the summer. With heaters and comfy furniture, you can enjoy it all year round.
Enjoy Hearty Meals:
Cooking outside opens up a world of delicious possibilities. You can make so much, from BBQ wings to kebabs and steaks. Outdoor cooking might even encourage you to eat healthier; nothing beats fresh food off the grill!
Expand Living Space:
Having an outdoor kitchen practically doubles your living area. You can invite many people over without worrying about space, whether for holidays, birthdays, or just big gatherings.
Keep Cooking Smells Away:
Some foods smell great when cooking, but others… not so much. These smells can stick around for days indoors. With an outdoor kitchen, you can cook those smelly foods outside, keeping your house smelling fresh and clean.
Save on Energy:
Surprisingly, having an outdoor kitchen can lower your electricity bill. When you cook inside during hot summers, your fans and AC must work harder to keep your house cool. Cooking outside gives your indoor systems a break, saving energy and money.
Cut Takeaway Costs:
Having an outdoor kitchen can also save you money when eating out. Instead of going to expensive restaurants, you can cook amazing meals at home. Even though setting up an outdoor kitchen costs money initially, your savings over time will outweigh the initial expenses. So, it’s like an investment rather than a waste of money.
Concluding Thoughts
An outdoor kitchen installation is a good idea and a worthy investment. You just need the right professionals to thoughtfully design it. So, contact Richard at Everest Siding and Windows .
Our certified installer oversees your initial consultation and the whole process from concept to completion. Call (832) 334-2528 to reach out.

## Is Pressure Washing Safe For All Surfaces?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/is-pressure-washing-safe-for-all-surfaces/
Updated: 2025-10-24
Summary: Learn which surfaces are safe for pressure washing and which ones to avoid. Learn simple tips to ensure safety and minimize damage risks.

Is Pressure Washing Safe For All Surfaces?
Apr 30, 2025
Pressure washing is a quick and effective process for cleaning stubborn dirt and grime from roofs, siding, and other exterior spaces, such as driveways. While it is considered super convenient, it might not always be a safe option for all surfaces.
In this blog, we will discuss which surfaces are safe for pressure washing and which ones require extra care or alternative cleaning methods.
Surfaces Considered Safe for Pressure Washing
Let’s list down some common surfaces that are generally considered safe for pressure washing.
Concrete and Brick
Concrete is one of the most durable and resistant materials. Pressure washing is ideal for washing off stains, dirt, and mildew from concrete surfaces. Brick can also handle pressure washing, though it’s best to use a lower setting and keep the nozzle at a safe distance to avoid cracking mortar.
Vinyl
Vinyl siding is designed to withstand harsh outdoor conditions, making it suitable for pressure washing. However, to avoid cracking or denting the panels, it is advised to use a lower pressure setting and a wide and downward spray tip.
Metal
Pressure washing is also considered safe for metal surfaces like aluminum and steel. Again, using the right pressure and nozzle is key to preventing scratches or dents.
Surfaces That Are NOT Considered Ideal For Pressure Washing
Pressure washing is not safe for all surfaces. Here are some options that fall in this list:
Wood
Wood is a soft material that is easily damaged due to high pressure and moisture retention. While many homeowners still opt for professional pressure washing, it is done with extreme care and caution, including a low-pressure setting and a wide fan tip.
Asphalt Shingles
Asphalt shingle roofs are a no-no for pressure washing. Extreme water pressure can loosen or remove shingles, leading to structural issues like leaking. Alternate cleaning methods, like soft washing, are recommended for these roofs.
Old Homes with Lead Paint
Old homes might have lead-based paint. Pressure washing risks dislodging this toxic material, releasing lead dust or paint fragments. In such cases, a professional inspection is advised for responsible washing.
Ensuring Safety While Pressure Washing
Pressure washing is a great option to remove debris buildup, if done correctly. Here are some tips to consider to ensure full safety:
Try pressure washing on a small hidden spot first, like a patch test
Start with the lowest pressure, especially on soft surfaces
Adjust pressure according to the cleaning needs
Use a wide-angle nozzle to reduce the risk of damage to different surfaces
Hold the nozzle 3–4 feet away from the surface
Use alternate cleaning methods i.e. soft washing, based on different materials
Overall Insight
Pressure washing is an excellent cleaning method. It provides quick and effective results leaving your home’s exterior shining. Some materials that are considered ideal for pressure washing are concrete, brick, vinyl, and metal. However, it is important to always adjust pressure settings to minimize damage risks.
We, at Everest Siding and Windows , provide safe and reliable pressure washing services in Houston, TX. Call us at (832) 334-2528 for prompt answers.

## Is Pressure Washing Safe for Roof Cleaning?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/is-pressure-washing-safe-for-roof-cleaning/
Updated: 2026-05-22
Summary: Are you thinking of pressure washing your roof? Find out how it can lead to damage, moss regrowth, and costly repairs.

Is Pressure Washing Safe for Roof Cleaning?
May 15, 2026
Cleaning a dirty roof is about more than just making the house look good; it is about making sure the building stays dry. Many people wonder if pressure washing is safe for roof cleaning when they see dark streaks or green growth taking over their shingles.
Let’s find out whether it is safe to use high pressure or if you are risking a major repair.
Why High Pressure Damages Your Shingles?
Most roofs use asphalt shingles covered in small mineral granules. These tiny rocks protect the asphalt from the sun and keep the roof from getting too hot. When you use a power washer, the force strips these granules right off. You will likely see them piling up in your gutters afterward.
Once these granules are gone, the shingles become thin and brittle. This leads to cracking and makes your roof wear out years earlier than it should. Without that protective layer, the sun’s heat breaks down the waterproofing, leaving your home vulnerable to the elements.
Can Pressure Washing Cause Roof Leaks?
Roofs are designed to shed water downward. It is not built to withstand water being fired at it from a side angle or from below. Using pressure washing can easily force water underneath the shingles. This moisture gets trapped against the wood decking and can stay there for a long time.
This trapped water often leads to wood rot or dampness in your attic. You might not notice the damage for months, but by then, the structural boards could be soft or covered in growth. Breaking the factory seals on your shingles also makes them much more likely to blow off in a storm.
Does Power Washing Remove Moss Permanently?
Power washing can damage shingles by stripping away protective granules and loosening the asphalt surface. It also creates tiny pits in the asphalt as it rips out the hold of moss and algae. Because this method doesn’t kill the invisible spores, the growth will quickly return to those damaged spots and start the cycle all over again.
What Is the Safer Alternative to Pressure Washing?
There is a much better way to handle this called soft washing. It uses a simple cleaning liquid that sits on the roof and kills the moss. There is no heavy pressure involved. This gets the roof clean without risking any of the structural damage that power washers cause.
Will Pressure Washing Void Your Roof Warranty?
Most roofing companies will cancel your warranty if you use a power washer. They know that high-pressure water can easily break or ruin shingles. By using a gentler cleaning method, you keep your insurance protection active. This helps you avoid paying for a brand-new roof all by yourself.
Why Should You Choose Professional Roof Cleaning Methods?
Professional cleaners adjust their solutions to match your roof’s specific needs. They use specialized equipment to reach every area without stepping on fragile shingles. This careful process provides a deeper, more even clean than standard DIY methods can achieve.
Experts identify hidden problems like loose shingles or early leaks during the cleaning process. Their tools ensure cleaning solutions reach deep into gaps to remove all debris. This thorough care prevents future damage and helps your roof last much longer.
Protecting Your Home Investment
In the end, your roof is far too important to risk for a fast clean. High-pressure water creates risks for leaks, rot, and shingle damage that are simply not worth the gamble. It is always better to use a gentle touch when it comes to your home’s main defense.
By choosing low-pressure cleaning methods, you ensure that your roof stays strong and waterproof for years to come. If you want to keep your home in top shape without the risk, reach out to Everest Siding and Windows . Contact us today at (832) 334-2528 to discuss the best care for your roof.

## Is Professional Gutter Cleaning Worth It?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/is-professional-gutter-cleaning-worth-it/
Updated: 2026-03-16
Summary: Wondering if professional gutter cleaning is really worth the cost? Discover how it saves you time, prevents costly water damage, and protects your home.

Is Professional Gutter Cleaning Worth It?
Jan 15, 2026
Many homeowners wonder if hiring a professional for gutter cleaning is really worth it when it seems like a simple job that they can manage on their own. But, to be honest, it is not as simple as it looks!
While professional gutter cleaning usually costs more, it often saves money in the long run by preventing serious water damage. Apart from cost, it also prioritizes safety, accountability, and longevity in results.
Read this blog to know why hiring professional gutter cleaning services is always worth it!
Benefits of Hiring a Professional
Gutter cleaning is not just about removing leaves and debris. Professionals do full-service gutter cleaning which includes the following:
Flush downspouts when needed
Perform a basic visual inspection for obvious issues
Spot early signs of damage that could affect your roof or foundation
They complete the entire process with great attention to detail, ensuring that no spot is left. They also have the right tools and experience to do the job safely and accurately. Gutter cleaning is not always as straightforward – professionals make sure they access tight and tricky spaces without compromising on safety.
Time and Convenience
Hiring a professional team for gutter cleaning saves a lot of time. They can clean the entire house’s gutter in 1 to 2 hours. In areas with lots of trees, professional cleaning also helps prevent pests like birds, insects, or rodents from nesting in clogged gutters. Hiring professionals does not require homeowners to chase after different vendors. It offers greater peace of mind.
Cost Differences
Professional gutter cleaning may seem expensive upfront, but it saves you money in the long run. They help extend the lifespan of your gutters, spot early problems, and recommend repairs where needed. Prices can vary by location, and some companies offer discounts for off-season cleanings or bundled services. You can compare prices of several companies to secure the best one.
When is Professional Gutter Cleaning Recommended?
Professional gutter cleaning is recommended for:
Multi-story or steep-roof homes
Heavy leaf buildup
Hard-to-reach gutters
Homes in wet or tree-heavy areas
Long-Term Value of Professional Gutter Cleaning
Regular gutter cleaning, once or twice a year, not just protects your gutters but also protects siding, foundation, and landscaping. During cleaning, professionals can look out for repairs that may compromise your gutter structure and cause water damage to your home. Well-maintained gutters “contribute to overall home condition and curb appeal. This short-term project has quite a lot of long-term benefits for homeowners.
Final Word
Professional gutter cleaning is usually worth it. It not only saves time on the client’s part but also makes sure that the job is done accurately and safely on the first go. Professionals bring in the right tools and experience to clean gutters. They ensure a thorough cleaning, catch problems if any, and recommend repairs to improve your gutter’s longevity.
If you are looking to clean your gutters, hire our expert team at Everest Siding and Windows . We provide gutter cleaning as an additional service. Call us at (832) 334-2528 to book a site visit.

## Mold: The Unseen Danger
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/mold-the-unseen-danger/
Updated: 2024-12-24
Summary: Explore how mold impacts health, identify hidden risks, and discover practical tips to keep your home mold-free.

Mold: The Unseen Danger
Aug 26, 2019
The unleashed destructive power of Harvey has left many of us heartbroken and wondering how and where to begin to put our lives back together and secure the safety of our homes. Besides the obvious visible issues that we need to address, there is another one, many times unseen, but extremely dangerous- mold.
The unprecedented amounts of water that poured over us for the past few days created a perfect environment for mold. There are a few facts that everybody, and especially homeowners, should know about molds.
What are molds?
Molds are fungi that can be found both indoors and outdoors. No one knows how many species of fungi exist but estimates range from tens of thousands to perhaps three hundred thousand or more. Molds grow best in warm, damp, and humid conditions- so our Houston climate is perfect for their proliferation, and spread and reproduce by making spores.
Where are molds found?
Molds are found in virtually every environment and can be detected, both indoors and outdoors, year round. Mold growth is encouraged by warm and humid conditions. Outdoors they can be found in shady, damp areas or places where leaves or other vegetation is decomposing. Many times, if the installation isn’t done correctly, they can be found behind siding. Roof water leaks can also lead to rapidly growing mold colonies in your attic or walls. Indoors they can be found where humidity levels are high, such as basements, attics, or showers.
How do molds affect people?
Mold is a major-league nuisance. It blackens the grout lines in your shower, discolors drywall, shows up as black spots on siding, darkens decks, and grows on and rots damp wood everywhere. Even worse, it can be bad for your health. It releases microscopic spores that cause allergic reactions, runny noses and sneezing, as well as irritating, even injurious, odors. Some people are more sensitive to molds than others. For these people, exposure to molds can cause symptoms such as nasal stuffiness, eye irritation, wheezing, or skin irritation. Some people, such as those with serious allergies to molds, may have more severe reactions. Severe reactions may occur among workers exposed to large amounts of molds in occupational settings, such as farmers working around moldy hay. Severe reactions may include fever and shortness of breath. Some people with chronic lung illnesses, such as obstructive lung disease, may develop mold infections in their lungs.
Should I be concerned about mold outside my home?
I have had customers that argued that mold can’t be prevented from landing on the exterior of their house, therefore they will not worry about it. I have politely disagreed because outside mold doesn’t always stay outside. For instance, mold on your roof may soon find its way into your attic. Mold can damage your home if starts growing under your siding. Some materials are more easily damaged by mold than others. Mold will literally eat away wood over time. Almost all materials will be damaged by mold to some extent given enough time, however, causing them to rot and fall apart.
Left unchecked, mold can cause damage great enough to lead to the collapse of ceilings, caving in of floorboards, and falling down of walls. Of course, it takes a while to reach that point. Your house is not going to fall down around you as soon as mold begins to grow in it. Many materials in the home quickly become damaged beyond the point of repair, though, and in time, a home can be completely destroyed by mold growth.
Children love to play outside, therefore they are particularly susceptible to mold-related health problems because their immune system is still developing. So mold around the areas they play is especially hazardous.
My house got flooded. Should I be concerned about mold?
After a storm or flood, mold can be a serious problem. I will focus on mold concerns outside the house since this is our specialty.
The starting point is to inspect the windows, siding, and roof to check if any of them became compromised. You can do the preliminary verification yourself, even though I do not recommend it because many times homeowners don’t know where or what to look for. Companies like Everest Siding and Windows will do a free inspection to analyze your situation and advise you if any mold concerns are real and you need to take further action. We will provide you with a written report documenting our findings and recommended course of action.

## Myths and Tips for Windows Replacement Projects
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/myths-and-tips-for-windows-replacement-projects/
Updated: 2024-01-29
Summary: There is so much information everywhere about replacing your windows that it can become very overwhelming at times.

Myths and Tips for Windows Replacement Projects
Aug 26, 2019
There is so much information everywhere about replacing your windows that it can become very overwhelming at times. However, a window replacement project need not be a difficult undertaking; just remember it pays to do your research before choosing a replacement window material or hiring a window installer. Learning more about the product as well as the process will help you find the windows that will best suit your home and make the project enjoyable and rewarding.
1. Replacing my windows will disturb the existing structure of my home.
Many people believe that a window replacement project requires extensive reconstruction, but generally this isn’t the case. Most good window installers can replace your windows without tearing out brick, sheet rock, or stucco. In addition, the majority of projects can be completed in two days without the need for extra stucco, sheet rock, or masonry work.
Tip:
Ask your window installer to explain their installation process to you so you will know what to expect.
2. Window replacement isn’t rocket science, anyone can do the job.
This is the biggest misconception that people have about window replacement. Installing windows is actually an acquired skill, so the more experience an installer has, the better the result will be. Several contractors will say that they can install windows, but not everyone can do it well.
A window will only function properly if installed right. A poorly set up window can be leaky, drafty, and difficult to open and close, among other things. Therefore it is important to do your research and find the right installer to ensure the long term performance of your new windows.
Again, ask your window installer questions regarding the project, and determine their level of comfort with carrying out the job before you hire them.
3. U-value is the most important factor in calculating the energy performance of a window.
U-value is the amount of heat transferred across a window. A lower U-value means that less heat passes through. While the U-value does measure the energy efficiency of a window, there are other factors that should be considered, such as visible light transmittance and solar heat gain coefficient (SHGC).
Your location also determines the significance of U-value to your situation. If you live in a colder climate, you will want to choose low U-value windows to keep the heat in your house from escaping. On the other hand, if you live in a warmer climate, the SHGC is more important as it measures the amount of solar heat that is transferred through a window. Windows with lower SHGC are better for houses in warmer climates.
U-value is more essential in colder climates because you want to capture as much of the sun’s radiant heat as possible.
4. I must use vinyl for my replacement windows.
Vinyl is the most popular material for replacement windows, but you have other options. If you live in an older home, you can substitute your current wood windows with more energy efficient clad/wood windows. These have a clad exterior, usually aluminum or vinyl, and a wood interior to match the appearance of your existing windows. The good thing about these windows is that they can usually be installed inside the “pocket” of your old windows without having to renovate your home.
Fiberglass is a newer replacement window material that has similar thermal properties to wood. It is also very durable and stronger than aluminum or vinyl. Fiberglass can be painted, so you have more color choices.
5. I don’t need safety glass if I don’t live in a coastal area
Many people think you are required to use safety glass only in coastal areas, but the truth is there are some areas in your house that requires it no matter where you are located. As a professional contractor, Everest Siding and Windows is aware of windows installation building codes and ensures your new windows installation project follows them for your protection.
Some areas in your home are required to have tempered glass, for instance if:
The glass is larger than 9 sq. ft. in total size
The bottom edge of exposed glass is within 18” from the floor or walking surface
The top edge of the glass is more than 36” from the floor or walking surface
There is a walking surface within 36” horizontally from the edge of the glass
Glass in a tub or shower-space when the bottom exposed edge of the glass is less than 60” from the walking or standing surface
Tempered glass is 4 to 5 times stronger than regular glass; it shutters in small pieces and less likely to cause injury. Make sure to ask your contractor if there are any areas in your home that requires the use of tempered glass.
6. MYTH: “A repaired window has no manufacturer’s warranty.”
Fact:
A damaged window usually loses its warranty, even if it is just a damaged nailing fin. However, many window manufacturers will extend their warranty if the VinylDoc method is used to repair the window. VinylDoc has repaired thousands of windows in which manufacturers’ warranties have been retained.
The reason they feel comfortable in maintaining their warranty is that VinylDoc, established in 1998, has proven the value of their repair method through time and quality. With that said, it is important to note that manufacturers will not warranty the repaired section. The person making the repairs is responsible for the warranty of their work.
7. MYTH: “A restored window is not as desirable as a new window. Only a new replacement window will appease the new homeowner.”
If replacement is a simple process and the window is inexpensive, it is better to replace the window. However, if replacing the window requires causes a major disturbance and expense, then a repair is the best option. Liability for home damage and scheduling multiple subcontractors, such as stucco, siding, sheetrock, carpenter, painter, etc. often makes window replacement problematic.
By contrast, a typical VinylDoc restoration can usually be completed in one day with minimal exposure to liability, inconvenience, noise or mess. When a window is repaired using the VinylDoc method and products, it will pass all the certification tests of a new window.
8. MYTH: “Broken nailing fins don’t need repair. On retrofit windows we just cut them off.”
A nailing fin is part of a permanent barrier designed to prevent water infiltration. Unless the window has been certified without nailing fins, it no longer meets the criteria for which it was tested. When nail fins fail, they can develop what is known as the ‘straw effect’ that draws water from outside to the inside of the house. Caulking does not solve the problem. Failure to repair the flange can lead to financial liability. More and more building inspectors are beginning to demand that broken nailing fins be addressed.

## Outdoor Living Trends for 2024
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/outdoor-living-trends-for-2024/
Updated: 2025-10-24
Summary: Here is a list of increasingly popular outdoor living trends for 2024. Incorporate them to create a bespoke space!

Outdoor Living Trends for 2024
Sep 30, 2024
As we progress in the modern world, our living styles also continue to change and evolve. One major change we are seeing is how outdoor living areas are becoming increasingly in demand – providing a full-of-life extension to our home.
Witnessing this appreciation for functional outdoor living space, let’s discuss popular trends that surround this topic!
Extending Indoor Spaces
Outdoor spaces like patios serve as an extension of your indoor living space. This transition of indoor and outdoor spaces is gaining momentum in 2024.
In order to build a physical boundary that alternates to a seamless outdoor – you can opt for sliding glass doors or retractable walls to create a cohesive environment. This allows homeowners to switch between spaces.
Comfortable Seating Areas
Comfort is the top most priority for homeowners curating an outdoor space. This has made up for a popular trend in 2024.
Whether you want to lounge with a book or host a bunch of friends, clients are looking to incorporate seating options which emulsify relaxation and conversation both. This may include plush sofas, armchairs or daybeds adorned with throws and cushions for added comfort.
Use of Organic Textures and Materials
For most homeowners, they need their outdoor living spaces to be aligned with nature. In lieu of this, organic materials and textures are making a comeback such as the use of natural wood, stone, rattan and bamboo.
These materials create a beautiful symphony between man-made furniture, nature and earthy elements.
Small Decks and Patios
In the year 2024, people are also reconceptualizing the utility of spaces. Whether you own a small outdoor living space, you can still make it work out using more intimate and cozy elements like multi-purpose or small sized furniture. The key is always to keep things simple.
Enclosed/Retractable Porches
Outdoor living spaces are becoming common day by day. Among the variety of spaces, we are now seeing – enclosed or partially covered patios back in trend. These offer a versatile option for people who are looking for protection/shade and still enjoy the beautiful outdoors. Another example for customizing the amount of shade you want in your outdoor spaces is retractable roofs.
Outdoor Kitchens
In order to curate a fully functional outdoor living space, outdoor kitchens are now the popular choice of homeowners. You can include built-in grills, pizza ovens, outdoor refrigerators and even small wine bars. This helps in elevating the whole dining experience and also allows hosts to interact with guests while enjoying the process of preparing delicious meals.
Brick Pavers
When we talk about outdoor living trends, brick pavers have remained a timeless choice. These are versatile, durable and even aesthetic. You can use this material for flooring and even making a statement wall. Brick pavers carry an unmatched nostalgia with them.
Final Words
Outdoor living spaces are now more than just an umbrella and a few chairs; they have become fully equipped extensions of our homes featuring comfortable seating, outdoor kitchens, retractable roof options and much more.
If you are looking to redesign your outdoor living space, contact Everest Siding and Windows for expert insight and hands-on skill. Call us at (832) 334-2528 to book our services.

## Payback – Renovations That Add Value To Your Home
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/payback-renovations-that-add-value-to-your-home/
Updated: 2024-12-24
Summary: Discover home renovations that boost value and offer great returns on investment with our expert tips and ideas.

Payback – Renovations That Add Value To Your Home
Aug 27, 2019
There are many renovation projects you can invest in that add significant value to your home. This includes both interior and exterior renovations, but did you know that you’re less likely to recoup your investment in a major kitchen or bathroom remodel than you are to get back what you spend on basic home maintenance such as new siding? So which home improvement projects should you invest in?
Continue reading to learn some of the top home improvement projects that will increase the value of your home and allow you to recoup a majority of your money.
Energy-Efficient Windows –
Older single-pane windows are a major turn off for prospective buyers. New energy-efficient windows can save you money on your heating and cooling costs by making your home energy efficient – which is what buyers are looking for. You might also qualify for additional credits from your state or even your utility company.
Adding a Wood Deck –
Outdoor living spaces have become more desirable and making your backyard more appealing by adding a wood deck can increase the value of your home. An inviting outdoor space for relaxing or hosting friends and family is at the top of prospective buyers lists.
Siding Replacement –
Damaged or deteriorating siding can date the look of your home, and not in a charming way. Updating your siding is a very valuable renovation that easily recoups the costs. Appraisers typically look at the structural elements of a home as part of their process and siding usually plays a part in that. Make sure not to neglect the trim – it’s an important factor in making your siding upgrade look its best.
New Garage Door –
This may not be the most exciting project but replacing your current garage door with an upgraded model will recoup almost 100% of the costs. Newer garage doors are those built with durable materials like steel, wood composites, and aluminum. They also have high-performance additions like energy-saving glazing and insulation.
At Everest Siding and Windows, we specialize in siding , windows , and more! If you are looking to make upgrades that add value to your home, turn to us! We will be able to give you advice and recommendations on what products will help your home become more energy-efficient, and help you save money on your energy bills. Contact us today to schedule a consultation!

## Should You Replace All Your Windows at Once or Do It in Phases?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/should-you-replace-all-your-windows-at-once-or-do-it-in-phases/
Updated: 2025-11-20
Summary: Decide whether to replace all your windows at once or in phases. Learn the benefits, costs, and tips to choose the best approach for your home.

Should You Replace All Your Windows at Once or Do It in Phases?
Nov 15, 2025
When it’s time to upgrade your home’s windows, one of the first decisions you’ll face is whether to replace them all at once or spread the project out over time. Both options work well; however, the right choice depends on your budget, schedule, and how quickly you want to see results.
Understanding the benefits of each approach can help you make the best decision for your home. So, let’s dive into the details of each of them!
Why Replace All Your Windows at the Same Time?
Many homeowners choose a full-home window replacement because it offers convenience and better value overall. When you replace every window in one go, your contractor can work more efficiently, which often lowers the cost per window. Replacing all windows at once often lowers your per-window installation cost due to labor efficiency. Some manufacturers or contractors may also offer volume-based pricing.
Replacing all windows at once maximizes overall home efficiency, but tackling the most damaged or drafty windows first can provide the largest immediate improvement. New windows provide better insulation, reduce heat loss, and can help reduce heating and cooling bills by 10–25%, depending on your home’s insulation, climate, and window type. If your current windows are old, drafty, or have broken seals, you’ll notice the difference in comfort immediately.
A full replacement also ensures a uniform look throughout your home (as long as the same style, trim, and finish are selected for all windows). Every room matches in style, trim, and finish, which improves both interior design and curb appeal. For homeowners planning to sell soon, this consistent appearance can make the house look newer and more polished.
Another major advantage is convenience. Instead of dealing with multiple installation appointments over months or years, the entire project is completed in one scheduled time frame. This minimizes disruption and lets you enjoy the benefits sooner.
Why Replace Windows in Phases?
If replacing all your windows at once isn’t realistic for your budget, phasing the project is a smart and practical alternative. Many homeowners choose this route so they can manage costs more comfortably and avoid a large upfront expense.
A phased approach also allows you to focus on the windows that need attention the most. For example, you may want to start with rooms that feel drafty, windows that no longer open properly, or areas exposed to harsh weather.
Spreading the project out also gives you flexibility. You can time certain phases around seasons—for example, replacing windows on the north side before winter—or coordinate with other renovations you’re already planning. Phased installation is also useful for homes with tricky access areas, such as second floors, additions, or rooms that require special equipment.
The key to a successful phased replacement is maintaining consistency. Using the same window style, color, and manufacturer helps ensure your home doesn’t end up with mismatched windows over time.
How to Decide What’s Best for Your Home
When choosing between full replacement and phasing, consider the following:
Current condition: Windows with rot, drafts, or failed seals should be replaced first.
Budget: Determine whether a single investment or phased spending works better for you.
Efficiency goals: If lowering energy bills is a priority, replacing more windows sooner will offer faster results.
Appearance: If you want a uniform, updated look right away, replacing everything at once is ideal.
Final Thoughts
Replacing all your windows at once offers the best overall value and a clean, consistent look. But if your budget or circumstances make that difficult, doing the job in phases is a perfectly effective option, as long as you plan it well and stick to the same materials and design.
Schedule window replacement services at Everest Siding and Windows . We promise quick, reliable, and transparent services. To book a site visit or request an estimate, call us at (832) 334-2528 .

## Siding Maintenance Tips: How To Keep Your Siding Looking Great
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/siding-maintenance-tips-how-to-keep-your-siding-looking-great/
Updated: 2025-09-11
Summary: Some siding maintenance tips include regular cleaning, avoiding harsh chemicals, inspecting mold, repairing cracks, and keeping the grill away.

Siding Maintenance Tips: How To Keep Your Siding Looking Great
Apr 15, 2024
Your home’s siding and roof work together to shield you from the weather, like rain, snow, and heat. While materials like vinyl can last a long time with little maintenance, others need more care.
No matter what your siding is made of, remember that you play a crucial role in its maintenance. Taking care of it will make it last longer and keep it looking nice.
Understand Your Siding Type
It is important to learn about the different kinds of siding materials your property might have. Each type has its own special features and maintenance needs.
Vinyl Siding:
Vinyl siding is easy to maintain and lasts a long time. It doesn’t rot, get damaged by water, or attract bugs. Just give it a gentle wash with soap and water now and then to keep it clean.
Wood Siding:
The wood siding looks beautiful but needs more care. You must paint or stain it regularly to protect it from water and sunlight, and you must check for damage or bugs often.
Fiber Cement Siding:
This siding is strong and doesn’t catch fire easily. Check it once a year for cracks or chips, and fix them quickly with a special cement paste.
Stucco Siding:
Stucco is tough and needs little upkeep. But it might get cracks over time, especially in places with changing temperatures. Seal any cracks you find to stop water from getting in.
Siding Maintenance Tips
Now that you understand the siding types and their unique natures. You are further ready to learn how to maintain each type with caution. Following are some helpful tips:
Cleaning Regularly
Wash your siding every six months to a year to keep it looking nice and lasting longer.
Use a soft brush and mild soap to gently scrub vinyl siding, then rinse with a garden hose.
Be careful if using a pressure washer and follow the instructions to avoid damaging the siding.
Avoid Harsh Chemicals
Don’t use strong chemicals like bleach or grease remover on vinyl siding, as they can damage it.
Also, avoid using abrasive scrubbers like steel wool, as they can fade the color and reduce water resistance.
Spot Mold and Mildew
If you see mold, clean it with a vinegar and water solution or a cleaner made specifically for vinyl.
But if you find dry rot or holes, it’s time to replace the siding.
Repair Cracks and Holes
Cracks and gaps in siding can let in moisture, leading to mold and rot. Fix them promptly to avoid bigger problems.
Avoid Painting Vinyl
While it’s possible to paint vinyl siding, it can void the warranty and cause damage. If you want a new color, it’s usually better to replace it.
Keep Grills Away
Don’t place grills too close to vinyl siding; the heat can melt or warp it. Keep grills at least 10 feet away on a non-flammable surface to prevent fires and damage to your siding.
Bottom Line
Remember that following the siding maintenance tips will secure your investment and leave your siding looking great for a long time. If you spot anything during your routine siding inspection, immediately call the professionals for repairs.
Contact our certified siding expert, Richard, and his team at Everest Siding and Windows . Our team is officially trained to install sidings according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Call us at (832) 334-2528 to book an appointment.

## Siding Replacement for Old Homes in Houston
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/siding-replacement-for-old-homes-in-houston/
Updated: 2026-03-25
Summary: Upgrade your old home with expert siding replacement in Houston. Durable materials, lifetime labor warranty, and trusted local installers.

Siding Replacement for Old Homes in Houston
Older homes across Houston have character you cannot replicate, but their siding often tells a different story. Years of heat, humidity, storms, and moisture slowly break down exterior materials. What looks like a small issue on the surface can quickly turn into deeper structural problems. Replacing siding on an older home is not just about appearance. It is about protecting the home, improving efficiency, and preserving its long term value.
Lets Talk!
Schedule Your Free Consultation!
Why Old Homes in Houston Need Siding Replacement
Houston’s climate is one of the toughest in the country for exterior materials. Constant humidity, heavy rain, and intense sun exposure accelerate wear and tear, especially on homes built decades ago.
Common problems include wood rot, swelling, mold growth, and pest damage. Many older homes still have original wood siding that was never designed to withstand modern environmental stress. Over time, paint stops protecting the surface, moisture gets trapped, and deterioration begins from the inside out.
If your home was built before the 1990s, there is a strong chance the siding has either reached the end of its lifespan or is no longer performing as it should.
Signs Your Old Home Needs New Siding
Homeowners often wait too long because the damage is not always obvious at first glance. Here are clear signs that replacement is the better option:
Warped or buckling boards
Soft spots or visible rot
Cracked or peeling paint that keeps returning
Mold or mildew on exterior walls
Higher energy bills without a clear reason
Frequent need for repairs
If multiple areas are affected, patching will only delay the inevitable. Full replacement becomes the smarter and more cost effective decision.
Why Repair Is Not Always Enough
With older homes, siding issues are rarely isolated. What looks like a small repair can be a sign of widespread moisture damage underneath.
Repairing sections may temporarily improve appearance, but it does not address hidden structural concerns. In many cases, mixing new materials with old siding creates uneven performance and reduces overall durability.
A full replacement ensures the entire exterior system works together, providing consistent protection and long term peace of mind.
Best Siding Options for Old Homes in Houston
Choosing the right material is critical, especially for older structures. The goal is to balance durability, appearance, and performance in Houston’s climate.
Fiber cement siding is one of the most popular choices. It resists moisture, does not rot, and holds up well against heat and storms. It can also be designed to match traditional architectural styles, making it ideal for historic homes.
Engineered wood siding is another strong option. It offers the natural look of wood but with improved resistance to moisture and pests. It is lighter than fiber cement, which can be beneficial for older framing.
Both options provide better longevity compared to traditional wood siding, while still maintaining the charm of an older home.
Structural Considerations for Older Homes
Replacing siding on an older home is not just a surface level project. It often reveals underlying issues that need attention.
Contractors may find water damage in the sheathing, outdated insulation, or framing that needs reinforcement. Electrical or plumbing adjustments may also be required depending on the condition of the walls.
This is why experience matters. Working on older homes requires a careful approach to avoid damaging original structures while upgrading performance.
Energy Efficiency Benefits
Older homes in Houston were not built with modern energy standards in mind. New siding installation is an opportunity to improve insulation and reduce energy loss.
With proper installation, homeowners often notice more consistent indoor temperatures and lower cooling costs. This is especially important in Houston where air conditioning runs for most of the year.
Upgrading siding can make your home more comfortable without changing its original character.
Maintaining the Look of a Historic Home
One of the biggest concerns homeowners have is losing the original charm of their property. The good news is that modern siding materials are designed to replicate traditional styles.
Whether your home has a classic wood lap look or a more detailed architectural design, replacement siding can be customized to match. Color options and textures allow you to preserve the visual identity of your home while upgrading its performance.
Cost Expectations for Siding Replacement in Houston
The cost of siding replacement for an older home can vary depending on size, condition, and material choice. Older homes may require additional work due to hidden damage or structural updates.
While the upfront investment may seem high, it prevents ongoing repair costs and protects the home from more expensive issues in the future. It also adds significant value if you plan to sell.
A professional inspection is the best way to understand the exact scope and cost for your specific home.
Final Thoughts
Replacing siding on an older home in Houston is one of the most important upgrades you can make. It protects your investment, improves energy efficiency, and preserves the beauty of your property.
Ignoring the problem only allows damage to spread. Taking action at the right time ensures your home stays strong, safe, and visually appealing for years to come.
If your siding is showing signs of age, now is the time to evaluate your options and make a decision that benefits your home long term. Working with a trusted company like Everest Siding and Windows can make the process smoother and more predictable, giving you confidence that your home is in capable hands from start to finish.

## Signs of Roof Damage Inside Your Home
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/signs-of-roof-damage-inside-your-home/
Updated: 2025-10-02
Summary: Learn how to spot roof damage from inside your home. Identify leaks, stains, and structural issues early to protect your property.

Signs of Roof Damage Inside Your Home
Jan 15, 2025
Inspecting your home for roof damage is crucial, even before visible signs appear. While a professional roofer can provide a detailed inspection, there are some signs you can spot yourself without climbing onto your roof. Here are common indicators of roof damage you might notice inside your home:
Water Leaks
Roof damage often allows water to seep under shingles or flashing. Even if it doesn’t drip directly into your living space, it can harm the roof deck or soak into insulation, creating the perfect conditions for mold.If water begins dripping inside, the damage may already be extensive, especially in the attic. Keep in mind, though, that not all leaks come from roof damage. They could also originate from water heaters or HVAC systems located in the attic.
Water Stains on Ceilings or Walls
Water stains typically appear as brown rings or streaks on walls or ceilings. These stains are caused by minerals left behind when water evaporates.However, they don’t always show up immediately. Stains may go unnoticed if your ceiling is dark or lighting is poor. A slow leak can lead to extensive damage before the stains become visible.
Peeling or Bubbling Walls or Wallpaper
Excess moisture can weaken the adhesive that holds up wallpaper, causing it to peel or bubble.This can lead to bubbling or peeling paint on your walls signifying roof damage.
Sagging Ceilings
When water pools in the attic, the weight can make the ceiling sag. Over time, this damage can worsen, and in severe cases, sections of the ceiling might collapse.
Wet or Damp Attic Insulation
Small leaks may not immediately drip into your home but instead get absorbed by the insulation in your attic.Over time, this moisture can compress the insulation, reducing its ability to keep your home warm. Mold can also grow in damp insulation, posing additional health risks.
Damp or Wet Attic Framing
Moisture in the attic can lead to condensation on the wood framing.This might be due to poor attic ventilation, water trapped beneath the roof shingles, or a combination of both. Wet wood can weaken over time, compromising your attic’s structure.
Musty or Damp Smells
If you notice a musty or damp smell in your attic, basement, or crawl spaces, it’s often a sign of moisture and possibly mold or mildew.This odor can develop even if you don’t see any visible signs of water damage. Mold can spread and cause serious issues if left unchecked.
Rising Energy Bills
If your insulation becomes wet, it loses its effectiveness, leading to higher heating or cooling costs.Wet fiberglass insulation may retain some water, lowering its efficiency. Cellulose insulation, which relies on trapped air for its insulating ability, flattens when wet, offering little to no protection.
Bottom Line
Moisture inside your home, whether visible or hidden, is a red flag for roof damage. If you notice water stains, peeling walls, sagging ceilings, or unusual smells, it’s time to investigate further.
A professional roofer at Everest Siding and Windows can help identify and repair the source of the problem, protecting your home from further damage. Call us at (832) 334-2528 to get an inspection scheduled.

## Signs You Need A Roof Replacement
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/signs-you-need-a-roof-replacement/
Updated: 2024-12-24
Summary: Discover the key signs that indicate it's time for a roof replacement and avoid costly repairs down the line.

Signs You Need A Roof Replacement
Aug 26, 2019
Don’t wait until your roof springs a leak!
You don’t have to wait until your roof starts to leak to find out you need a roof replacement. There are many signs that your roof might be on its way out. By knowing the signs and frequently checking your home for problems, you can get ahead of your roof – meaning that you might be able to have your roof replaced before dealing with the hassle of a leak.
Check out the signs below, and if you think you might need your roof replaced, call us today!
Believe it or not, the first place to check isn’t the outside of your home, but the attic, or highest point of your home if you don’t have one. Be sure to take notice of any light coming in through the roof, as it signals a problem.
Check to see when the last time the roof was completely replaced. A typical asphalt shingle roof lasts for 20-25 years before needing to be replaced. Metal roofs last longer on average.
If your roof is comprised of shingles, check for damage periodically, especially following a storm. Shingles should lie flat against the roof. If you see cracks or buckling, call a roofing contractor for repairs. While you’re up there, be sure to also check the gutters for any shingle granules.
If there is a chimney or skylight on your roof, flashing is used to seal the roof. Like the shingles, the flashing must be periodically inspected for damage as well. If you notice any cracking or breaking, give us a call.
Moisture damage can lead to mold growth and rotting boards, both of which means trouble for your roof. Check the roof for signs of moisture, mold, or rotting, especially at the low points. Moss can be cleaned using a stiff brush, but the underlying cause of the mold growth must still be dealt with
If you notice any signs of damage on your roof, or if you need some help determining if what you’re seeing is a cause for concern, call Everest Siding and Windows today. We serve all of Greater Houston.

## Summer Care Tips For Your Outdoor Space
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/summer-care-tips-for-your-outdoor-space/
Updated: 2024-09-19
Summary: Consider the following summer care tips for your outdoor space. Call professionals in case of any help!

Summer Care Tips For Your Outdoor Space
Sep 15, 2024
Summer is the best season to enjoy the outdoors. Whether you want to bask in the sun, prepare for a pool party, or just spend quality playtime with your children, your outdoor space should be inviting and well equipped to enhance your summer experience.
In order to achieve an overall outdoor experience, we will list down some basic home improvement ideas – that aid both style and function outside your home premises.
Summer Lawn Care
Unkempt grass and lawns can throw you off. They not only look unappealing but can also be breeding grounds for pests, ticks, and insects.
For best results, you must research the type of grass, its length, and optimal cutting length. If you are unsure about the following, you can always seek professional help.
Planting Beds
Many annual plants, like petunias, impatiens, geraniums, and marigolds, bloom all summer. To keep them looking their best, regularly trim off any dead blooms so new flowers can grow.
Also, consider setting aside a space in your garden for a summer kitchen garden. You can grow easy herbs, tomatoes, and peppers to enjoy fresh produce throughout the season.
Decks, Patios, Terraces
These outdoor spaces can provide a warm and welcoming outdoors in summer. They serve as an extension of your home.
In order to care for your outdoor space, make sure to deep clean the area to remove debris and mold.
Inspect the area for any wood rot, loose nails and other repairs or replacements to make sure your outdoor space does not run into costly problems.
Outdoor Furniture
Most outdoor furniture is designed to handle different weather conditions thanks to its durable materials. To keep it looking great, dust and clean it regularly using a mild soap and water solution.
For outdoor upholstery, use the same solution to scrub it, and then let it air dry in the sun. Avoid machine washing cushion covers, as this could affect their shine.
Irrigation Systems
Whether you use an underground sprinkler system or a sprinkler head attached to your garden hose, learning the right watering techniques can save you considerable time and money. Research about the best practices or talk to fellow neighbors about what works best for them!
Water your lawn early in the morning or late in the evening to reduce evaporation.
Aim for deep, infrequent watering rather than shallow, frequent watering.
Ensure sprinkler heads are adjusted to cover the lawn evenly without wasting water on sidewalks or driveways.
Regularly inspect your system for leaks or malfunctions and address them promptly to avoid water wastage or soil erosion.
If possible, use a timer to regulate watering times and avoid overwatering.
Grilling and Outdoor Kitchen
In order to keep those barbecue nights in function, make a habit to deep clean the grill gates, gas burners and other kitchen elements.
This helps reduce the chances of any mess or build-up considering best hygiene practices.
Final Words
Outdoor cleaning and maintenance is an integral part of home maintenance. At Everest Siding and Windows , we provide specialized expertise and distinctive outdoor living services. So, what are you waiting for? Call us at (832) 334-2528 to book our services.

## Summer Home Maintenance Tips
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/summer-home-maintenance-tips/
Updated: 2025-10-02
Summary: Ensure your home stays safe and efficient this summer with expert siding, window, and maintenance tips from Everest Siding & Windows

Summer Home Maintenance Tips
Jun 15, 2024
Summer home improvement remains a mission for many homeowners. People opt for seasonal repairs to keep ready for the entire season. Summers can necessitate many things at your home. This is mainly important to ensure everything in your house is in working condition. In this blog we will share some highly recommended home maintenance tips for our readers to build a checklist for them.
Why Is Summer Home Maintenance Important?
While home maintenance is essential for every home. Why does summer become a factor to consider? Let’s unpack.
Regular maintenance helps address potential issues before they become a hazard and costly repair.
Proper maintenance ensures that air conditioning and insulation is working properly.
This also increases home value and is important when you are planning to put your house on sale.
Regular checks can prevent incidents of fire.
Enhances the comfort of living spaces.
Home maintenance can help you check signs of pests and infestation.
Summer is a great time for new landscaping which can improve the aesthetic and function of your house.
Let’s List Some!
Clean Your Gutter
A great way to start your summer home maintenance is to clean your gutters and downspouts. Summers can bring in extreme weather which may require gutter cleaning as a top priority work. This can ensure that your gutters will withstand harsh weather such as monsoon during summers. This also helps keep together your home’s integrity.
Wash Siding and Windows
Wash your exterior windows siding and screen by removing and scrubbing them with a soap and gentle scrub with hot water. This gives your home a clean and finished look. examine your doors and windows and seal tightly and function properly to maintain optimum temperature from your air conditioning. If your home is not equipped with central air, check for cooling tips online.
Clean Your Outdoor Living Spaces
Summer calls for a fresh and clean outdoor environment for homeowners. Which is why it is suggested to inspect and clean your sidewalks, driveway, patio and deck. Use a pressure washer to clean dirt. Check for cracks or weeds there. Once you have inspected everything, wash away all the dirt for the summer.
Beautify Your Yard
As summer arrives, you want to make your yard look beautiful and fresh. This is why it is important to check that your yard is free from pests and insects. A professional spritz of pest control spray can go a long way. Remove dead plants, trim overgrown trees and make your back/front yard ready for summer gatherings or pool parties with some new and old landscaping.
Check Your HVAC System
Checking whether your air conditioning is working fine is crucial in summers. This ensures a comfortable environment for homeowners.
Roof Cleaning
Regardless of your weather, roof cleaning is essential for homeowners on an annual basis. You might want to call for professional roof cleaning services to ensure that it is in good working conditions.
Final Words
Summer home maintenance is important to ensure that all your residential components are working fine for the upcoming season. Are you in need of professional summer home maintenance? Call Everest Siding and Windows for inspection and quality service. Call us at (832) 334-2528 .

## The Perfect Shade: Choosing a Siding Color
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/the-perfect-shade-choosing-a-siding-color/
Updated: 2024-12-24
Summary: Discover the ideal siding color for your home with tips on style, curb appeal, and long-lasting beauty.

The Perfect Shade: Choosing a Siding Color
Aug 26, 2019
Are you thinking about changing the color of your home? Maybe your current siding has seen better days? Changing the look of your home can be exciting, but also overwhelming. With an entire scheme of colors to choose from, selecting just one to be on your home for the foreseeable future can be a hard decision to make. Not only does the color of your home set the entire tone, it affects the way you feel and showcases your personality.
WHEN YOU CHOOSE THE NEW COLOR SCHEME FOR YOUR HOME, YOU’LL WANT TO CONSIDER A FEW DIFFERENT THINGS:
Color Wheel- Do you want analogous (colors right next to each other on the color wheel) or complementary (colors opposite on the wheel) colors?
Warm or Cool- Depending on what tone you want for your home, this is an excellent way of narrowing down the options. Reds, yellows, and oranges are considered warm, while blues, purples, and greens are cool.
Number of color options- Do you have shutters, a garage, or a porch/ deck that you plan on coordinating with the siding color? If you like the existing color of those, choosing the siding based on those colors makes it easier.
Trim Color- Do you have a lighter or darker trim color that you want to complement the siding?
Neighborhood/ Environment- Do you want to stand out or coordinate with the rest of the neighborhood? Maybe you’re looking for the color to look good with the foliage/environment.
It may seem like a lot to choose the color of your home, but it really comes down to what draws you in more. Consider what types of colors attract you most on other homes or in general. If you struggle to choose your colors, you could also benefit from a free color consultation with a color specialist through our partnership with Sherwin Williams.
We’re here to help!
Whether you choose LP SmartSide or HardiePlank siding , Everest Siding and Windows is here to help! Give us a call today to schedule a free, in-home consultation. (832) 334-2528

## Thinking DIY For Your Siding Installation? Think Again!
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/thinking-diy-for-your-siding-installation-think-again/
Updated: 2024-12-24
Summary: Considering DIY for your siding installation? Think again! Discover why professional installation is the smarter choice.

Thinking DIY For Your Siding Installation? Think Again!
Aug 26, 2019
Learn why hiring a professional is your best option.
DIY-ing can be the best idea you’ve ever had, or it can be the worst and come back to haunt you. Most DIY-ers who take on small projects around the house think they can take on much bigger, more complicated tasks, too. Some might succeed, but more often than not, they fail. We don’t want this to happen to you!
If you’re an avid DIY-er who’s looking to install their own siding, we kindly suggest you stick to the small jobs, instead. Though it might seem like the cheaper, faster way to get the job done, it could backfire.
Read about all the reasons why DIY vinyl siding installation is not the best idea.
Cost
You might think that doing the job yourself will be cheaper, but you could be wrong. Sure, you won’t have to pay for the cost of labor, however, you’ll have to buy all the materials, tools, and equipment needed for the job. This can add up quickly, and if you don’t spend the money on the right tools and equipment, or those of high-quality, you could end up with a subpar or improper installation. It pays to pay for the labor of a professional and their team who come fully equipped for the job. It might even end up being cheaper by hundreds of dollars or just a few, but regardless, it could be cheaper!
Experience
Have you ever installed siding before? If all you’ve been doing is watching YouTube videos, you’re going to need a little more “expertise” than that! Vinyl siding installation involves several different steps and lots of attention to detail to ensure the utmost accuracy. Hire a professional with experience for the utmost precision to ensure the siding is installed correctly and lasts a long time.Labor
Doing the job yourself can end up taking a lot longer than expected. Things like your full-time job, kids, school events, social life, weather, and other factors can get in the way of you completing your project on time. By hiring a professional, the job can get done in a fraction of the time!
