## Types Of Covered Patios Suitable For Your Home
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/types-of-covered-patios-suitable-for-your-home/
Updated: 2024-08-08
Summary: Assess the style and decorative needs of your home for your covered patio and call us for professional advice!

Types Of Covered Patios Suitable For Your Home
May 15, 2024
On a sunny bright Sunday, as you look forward to lounge in your patio with a cup of cold coffee and a good book – direct scorching heat has some other plans for you. While you want to soak the sun, but also want some shade to enjoy the outdoors, covered patios can be suitable for your home!
What is a Patio?
A patio is an outdoor space, a seeming extension of your house. This space is situated in the backyard or garden – and comes in a variety of sizes and designs depending on your house layout. Patios are typically made of flat, paved material such as concrete, stone, brick or tiles.
In addition to that, patios serve a multi-functional purpose, depending on how you want to curate the space. While some reserve it as a dining recreational space, others might like it to be a purely lounging area.
The idea of the space is to create an outdoor area reserved for miscellaneous activities. Some might like it to be completely open-air, while others might like it covered or partially enclosed depending on their vision and preferences.
Few Benefits of Covered Patios
Covered patios are now available in multiple types and provide the most feasible way to enjoy the outdoors. The shaded region – whether full or partial – protects against harmful UV rays and provides shelter from rain and snow. Not only that, covered patios also protect your patio furniture and decorative pieces.
It also adds to the overall appeal and functionality of your residential property – as a categorical outdoor living space. Covered or semi-covered patios provide a versatile area where you can channel your individuality while arranging intimate family dinners, friend’s karaoke night, or a weekend movie night with your partner or friends.
Types of Covered Patios
If you are planning to make shelter related changes to your patio, here are some types of covered patios to consider!
Awnings: Awnings are basically a sheet of canvas or other material that functions as a stretched, downward frame to keep sunlight and rain away. As a homeowner, you have the choice to keep them as permanent fixtures or retractable. They are a convenient, long-lasting, and highly customizable choice.
Pergolas: Pergolas provide a classic yet modern type of covered patio – with equally spaced rafters or completely solid. Pergola styles can be determined according to your property needs such as free-standing, attached, or hanging. They offer extensive options and are strong enough to support light fixtures. Pergolas are generally low maintenance depending on the material i.e. metal, vinyl, wood, etc.
Solar Screens: Solar screens are fabric panels that act as curtains for your outdoor patio. The primary function of a solar screen is to block sunlight and absorb heat. Installing these fixtures can help manage sunlight in peak hours and provide privacy when needed.
Shaded Sails: If you are looking for a portable patio cover, shade sails can be a perfectly suited covering option. Not only do they prevent sun rays, but they are waterproof and provide an edge on affordability. You can choose to keep, remove, or adjust, depending on your needs.
Factors To Consider Before Choosing a Patio Cover
Thinking about these factors will help you make the right choice for you and your home since there are numerous types of covered patios available to choose from.
Overall budget
Outdoor weather conditions
Overall residential appeal
Total square feet of patio
Maintenance cost
Final Words
There are a variety of styles, designs, and materials that fall under the category of covered patios. From wood, vinyl and metal choices, manual and automated, to fixed and retractable – assess your needs and budgets for a covered patio makeover.
Discuss your ideas with Everest Siding and Windows for comprehensive outdoor living services in Houston, TX . Call us at (832) 334-2528 to book an appointment.

## Upgrade to Vinyl Double-Pane Low-E Windows
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/upgrade-to-vinyl-double-pane-low-e-windows/
Updated: 2026-10-06
Summary: Replace old aluminum windows with vinyl double-pane Low-E glass for lower energy bills, less noise, and a more comfortable home year-round.

Upgrade to Vinyl Double-Pane Low-E Windows
Sep 30, 2026
Old single-pane aluminum windows tend to show their age in more ways than one. They let heat escape, let noise in, and rarely look as good as they used to. Replacing them with vinyl double-pane Low-E windows is one of the more practical upgrades a homeowner can make, and the benefits go beyond just looks. Here’s a breakdown of what actually changes once you make the switch.
Why Double-Pane and Low-E Glass Work Together
Double-pane windows use two layers of glass with a sealed gap in between, usually filled with air or an inert gas. That gap acts as a buffer, slowing down how quickly heat moves through the glass. So in summer, less heat gets in. In winter, less heat gets out.
Low-E coating adds another layer of performance. It’s a thin coating on the glass that reflects infrared heat and cuts down on UV exposure, without making the room feel darker or the glass feel tinted. On their own, double-pane glass and Low-E coating each help. Used together, double-pane construction and Low-E glazing can provide greater thermal performance than a single-pane window without Low-E glazing.
Why Vinyl Frames Make Sense
Aluminum frames conduct heat, which works against everything the glass is trying to do. They also corrode over time and need repainting. Vinyl doesn’t have either problem. It insulates better and holds up with minimal upkeep, which matters if you’d rather not think about your windows every few years.
What Homeowners Actually Notice
The difference usually shows up in small, everyday ways:
Rooms stay a more even temperature, room to room
Drafts near windows mostly disappear
Energy bills often trend lower
Outside noise is noticeably reduced
Less dust and pollen work their way in
Part of this comes down to the seal. Older aluminum windows tend to develop small gaps over time, and that’s usually where drafts, noise, and dust find their way in. A tighter seal on new windows helps close that gap, literally.
Curb Appeal and Resale Value
New windows also change how a house looks from the outside, which isn’t nothing when you’re trying to sell or just want the place to look cared for. Real estate agents often point to windows as one of the upgrades buyers notice, though how much value it adds really depends on the market, the home, and a handful of other factors that vary case by case.
Is It Worth the Investment?
With energy costs an ongoing concern for most homeowners, upgrading to windows built for better efficiency is a reasonable long-term move. Results vary depending on your climate, your home’s size, and how well-insulated it already is, but vinyl double-pane Low-E windows are a solid option if you’re looking to cut down on energy waste and improve comfort at the same time.
Thinking About New Windows?
If your current windows are past their prime, Everest Siding and Windows can help you find the right vinyl double-pane Low-E option for your home and budget. Call (832) 334-2528 to set up a consultation and see what upgrading could look like for your house.

## Vinyl Window Life Expectancy: How Long Do They Last?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/vinyl-window-life-expectancy-how-long-do-they-last/
Updated: 2026-03-18
Summary: Vinyl windows are everlasting. They tend to have a life expectancy of about 20 to 40 years as long as it isn’t exposed to bright sunlight.

Vinyl Window Life Expectancy: How Long Do They Last?
Mar 15, 2026
If you’re thinking about upgrading your house but don’t know where to start, try getting your windows done first. Not only do they make your house stand out, but they also protect your house from danger, although that depends on the type of windows you get.
These days, vinyl windows are getting all the recognition, and that too, for good reason! Given how affordable they are and how little maintenance is required, almost everyone wants to switch to them. Plus, with vinyl windows, you don’t have to worry about applying a new layer of tint on top.
But when making a switch as big as swapping windows, the one thing homeowners worry about is the life expectancy, and when it comes to vinyl windows, you can expect them to last for a very long time! To learn more about them and their features, make sure to keep reading this blog till the end.
What Are Vinyl Windows?
Vinyl windows are made from polyvinyl chloride (PVC), a synthetic resin material that is known to be extremely durable and rust-proof. However, the one aspect that makes vinyl windows stand out is the way they are constructed.
With multiple chambers fitted in a single frame, vinyl windows provide much-needed insulation. Not to mention, they are energy-efficient, which means they’re safe for the environment. Additionally, homeowners have the option to choose from the variety of styles, colors, and designs they come in.
What is The Average Life Expectancy of a Vinyl Window?
On average, vinyl windows can last for up to 20 to 40 years. However, that is primarily if you take good care of them and maintain them over time. When compared to other materials, such as wood or aluminum, vinyl windows easily have the highest life expectancy.
It is also important to note that the lifespan of a window varies for everyone. Factors such as where you live, the climate, the area of the house, etc., all play a big role in determining how long it will last. For instance, if you live in an area that gets a lot of direct sunlight or is very hot throughout the year, chances are you might need window replacement more frequently than those living in colder climates.
Factors That Affect The Lifespan of a Vinyl Window
Believe it or not, there are several factors that influence the longevity of vinyl windows. Some of the most prominent factors include:
Window Material
High-quality vinyl windows with reinforced frames and premium design tend to have a longer lifespan compared to lower-quality alternatives.
Installation Charges
Getting your vinyl windows installed by experienced professionals guarantees that they will function properly and will be able to stand the test of time.
Care and Maintenance
Regular cleaning and maintenance can boost the lifespan of vinyl windows. Maintenance aspects like lubricating hinges and cleaning tracks can prevent the windows from deteriorating, extending their durability.
Final Takeaway
All in all, the average life expectancy of a vinyl window ranges from 20 to 40 years with proper maintenance and care. Factors such as quality, installation, maintenance, and climate influence how long vinyl windows last. So, if you also want your windows to be strong and durable, why not switch them up? Contact the experts at Everest Siding and Windows for more information at (832) 334-2528 .

## Vinyl Windows and the Environment
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/vinyl-windows-and-the-environment/
Updated: 2024-12-24
Summary: Explore how vinyl windows contribute to energy efficiency and sustainability, benefiting both your home and the environment.

Vinyl Windows and the Environment
Aug 26, 2019
Vinyl windows have less impact on the environment than most competitive materials.
Less than half of vinyl’s weight is dependent on natural resources.
Vinyl window manufacture requires only one-third of the energy needed to manufacture aluminum windows.1
Vinyl windows’ long term durability and low maintenance don’t require the use of additional resources, ie. paint or stain — for upkeep and repair as do competitive materials. Cleanup and disposal of paints and stains are also avoided.
How Vinyl Windows Are Made
Like all plastic materials, vinyl window frames are made by changing hydrocarbon-based raw materials (petroleum, natural gas or coal) into unique synthetic products called polymers. The polymer that makes vinyl windows is unusual, however, because it is based only in part on hydrogen and carbon. Rigid polyvinyl chloride (vinyl) possesses excellent fire performance properties. In particular, it will not support combustion.
After the vinyl resin is produced, the manufacture of vinyl windows and their installation follow three basic steps. First, the window frames are made through a process called extrusion that combines heat and pressure to form the vinyl resin into the desired shapes. Second, the vinyl frames are cut to the desired size and assembled with glass and hardware into a completed window unit. Finally, the window units are installed in the home.
Vinyl Windows Are Easy on the Environment
The stability and inert nature of the vinyl polymer keep vinyl windows in service for many years. Because of the long term color and property retention, homeowners avoid the vapor emission, cleanup and disposal problems associated with frequent application of certain paints and stains.
Vinyl is readily recycled. When vinyl components are formed during the extrusion process, product changeovers (for different colors and frame parts) and new product start-ups require different operating conditions that may produce some scrap. This scrap can be reclaimed and recycled back into the manufacturing process or into other plastic products, such as pipe.
During the window assembly process, materials are cut to length and welded or mechanically fastened into window sashes and frames. Manufacturers’ high-tech, computer-controlled equipment optimizes cutting efficiency and minimizes waste. The small amount of scrap generated can be recycled into other plastic products.
Vinyl Windows Save Energy During the Manufacturing Process
In terms of the total amount of energy needed to take a product from raw materials to market, a 1991 study conducted by Franklin Associates showed that vinyl windows required considerably less energy to manufacture than windows made from competitive materials, particularly aluminum. In fact, according to the study, the manufacture and use of vinyl windows (compared to the energy costs required if wood and aluminum were used as alternative framing materials) saves the U.S. nearly 2 trillion Btu’s every year — enough energy to meet the yearly electricity needs of 20,000 single family homes, or the equivalent of 16 million gallons of gasoline.
Vinyl Windows Help Conserve Energy and Reduce Home Heating and Cooling Costs
Because vinyl windows are not good conductors of heat or cold, they provide superior insulation during both winter and summer season. The combination of vinyl’s excellent insulation properties and specially designed insulating air spaces makes vinyl frames a formidable barrier to heat transfer. Tests using a common measure of insulating ability (U-value) have shown that vinyl windows regularly outperform competitive products. Vinyl windows keep the warm air in during the winter and the cool air in during the summer. Energy is conserved and money is saved when the furnace and air conditioners work less to maintain the desired temperature.
In fact, using conservative national averages, upgrading to double glazed, energy efficient all-vinyl windows could save a homeowner more than $30 a month during the coldest part of the winter. Further, in recognition of excellent energy performance, many utility companies across the nation are offering builders cash incentives to install vinyl windows. For example, under its Energy Partnership Program, San Diego Gas & Electric provides an average of $600 to builders who switch from aluminum to vinyl windows in 2,000 square foot homes. Consumers should check with local utility companies for details and requirements.
Vinyl Windows are the Clear Choice for Your Home, and Our Environment
The facts are in. In terms of energy consumption and maintenance, vinyl windows represent a wise investment. Their superior insulating capability allows homeowners not only to conserve energy, but to save more on heating and cooling costs as well. Vinyl’s long-term endurance and recyclability also support vinyl windows as a sound environmental choice. More and more Americans are selecting vinyl windows for their homes. U.S. sales of vinyl windows currently exceed 16 million units each year, with continued growth expected.
It is clear that vinyl windows are a smart choice from a cost and maintenance perspective. It is also apparent that vinyl windows are the clear choice for not only energy and cost-conscious homeowners, but the environmentally-aware as well.
The environment is something we at Everest are very sensitive to, as you will see from our preferred products such as vinyl windows and LP SmartSide siding .

## What are Solar Attic Fans and Why do You Need Them?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/what-are-solar-attic-fans-and-why-do-you-need-them/
Updated: 2024-12-24
Summary: Learn what solar attic fans are and how they can help improve energy efficiency, reduce cooling costs, and protect your home.

What are Solar Attic Fans and Why do You Need Them?
Aug 26, 2019
Solar attic fans are becoming increasingly popular in homes today. But what exactly are they? And why should you have one in your home? Keep reading to find out what a solar attic fan does and why it makes sense to have one in your home.
What is it?
First, we’ll talk about what a solar attic fan is. Okay, if you have a two-story home, does the upstairs sometimes get uncontrollably warm during the summer months? Do you find it more difficult to keep the upstairs cool compared to downstairs? This is where a solar attic fan comes in to play. A solar attic fan pulls out superheated air from your attic (this superheated air is often the reason why it is so difficult to cool the upstairs of your home) and replaces it with cooler air from outside. Make sense? Essentially, a solar attic fan is replacing superheated air with cooler air; resulting in a cooler upstairs of your home.
Why Should you Buy a Solar Attic Fan for your Home?
The first reason why you should invest in a solar attic fan is fairly obvious. We point directly at the main purpose of the solar attic fan. Its main purpose is to help the upstairs of your home cool off easier by replacing superheated air from your attic with cooler air from outside. So the number one advantage of a solar attic fan is that your upstairs will be much easier to cool.
The second and final reason why you should buy a solar attic fan relates to the first reason. What is a direct result of it being easier to cool the upstairs of your home? You guessed it… you’ll save money! Granted, it might only be as much as $50-$60 worth of saving each year, but every little bit counts!
Ultimately, the main reason why you should invest in solar attic fans is the added comfort it will bring to your home. Gone are the days when being upstairs in your home meant sitting in uncomfortable heat. With solar attic fans you can now enjoy the upstairs of your home just as much as the downstairs. This reasoning increases ten fold if your bedroom is located on the upper floor of your home. Who wants to be uncomfortably hot while they sleep? Answer… NO ONE. So, if you sleep upstairs at home, then you absolutely need a solar attic fan.
If you have any questions about solar attic fans or any of our other products/services, give us a call today!

## What Causes Siding To Fade?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/what-causes-siding-to-fade/
Updated: 2025-10-24
Summary: Siding can fade due to several reasons like sun exposure, material quality, weather, debris accumulation, and improper maintenance.

What Causes Siding To Fade?
May 15, 2025
Siding covers a significant part of your home exterior. However, it is susceptible to damage overtime in the form of fading. If you notice that your siding is losing color or appears patchy and dull, read this blog to learn the reasons and how you can address them.
Reasons Why Your Siding Is Fading
Siding can fade due to several reasons. Here are some:
Sun Exposure
The primary reason why your siding is fading is due to prolonged exposure to sunlight. UV rays tend to break pigments in siding materials, causing them to lose their original color and vibrancy. This is most common in south- and west-facing walls, which receive more sunlight throughout the day.
Even high-quality siding material can fade over the years. However, specialized UV treatments can make it last longer.
Material Quality
Low-quality siding material can exhibit signs of fading faster than high-grade and premium materials. Low-quality materials have weaker pigmentation and less durable protective coatings, putting them at an increased risk of damage.
Hence, investing in high-quality material is always recommended to extend your siding’s lifespan without any signs of wear.
Weather and Environmental Factors
The weather has a big impact on how siding fades over time. Rain, snow, hail, and changes in temperature can slowly damage the siding’s surface. Moisture can get inside, causing mold, mildew, or algae to grow, which makes the siding look discolored and faded.
In some places, acid rain or salty air can accelerate fading by removing protective layers and allowing the UV rays to cause more damage.
Pollution and Chemicals
Your siding constantly interacts with dirt, debris, and other airborne pollutants. These can lead to discoloration over time. Additionally, harsh cleaning chemicals or abrasive tools can also damage the siding finish, leading to fading.
Improper Maintenance
Regular maintenance is the key to preventing your siding from fading. Dirt, grime, and things like mold or algae can build up and hold in moisture, which makes UV damage worse. Hiring professional siding cleaning services helps get rid of stubborn spots and keeps it looking good.
Addressing and Preventing Faded Siding
While some degree of fading is inevitable, here are some steps you can take to address the issue and prevent damage:
Pick quality siding material with UV-resistant colors and strong protective coatings to prevent premature fading
Hiring professional help to wash your siding gently at least once a year to remove dirt, mold, and pollutants
If your siding is faded but still in good condition, repaint it with high-quality, UV-resistant paint to bring its shine
If only some panels are fading, replacing those sections can be a cost-effective solution
Adding a clear sealant or protective coating helps prevent fading and keeps your siding looking great for years
If your siding is damaged beyond repair, replacement might be necessary
Final Word
Siding materials are prone to fading due to several reasons like prolonged sun exposure, material quality, weather, air pollutants, and improper maintenance. While some degree of fading over years is inevitable, using high quality material, professional cleaning, repainting, resealing and prompt repairs that help your siding to last long.
Want to address siding issues? Call Everest Siding and Windows at (832) 334-2528 for reliable solutions.

## What Is Soft Wash Roof Cleaning?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/what-is-soft-wash-roof-cleaning/
Updated: 2026-10-28
Summary: Soft wash roof cleaning uses low-pressure water and safe cleaning solutions to remove dirt, moss, and moisture without damaging your roof.

What Is Soft Wash Roof Cleaning?
Mar 30, 2025
Your roof can accumulate dust and debris over time. This is where professional roof cleaning comes in. The two main types include soft wash and pressure wash. In this blog, we will specifically talk about soft-wash roof cleaning, how it works, and its benefits.
What Does Soft Wash Roof Cleaning Mean?
Soft-wash roof cleaning is a safe and effective way to clean roofs. It uses low-pressure water and eco-friendly cleaning solutions to remove dirt, algae, and moss growth on roofs. Unlike traditional pressure washing, which can damage the roof, soft washing provides a safer, long-lasting solution for cleaning roofs.
How Does It Work?
The process starts with a thorough roof inspection. Afterward, a biodegradable detergent is sprayed on the roof using a low-pressure nozzle. The cleaning solution is made to sit for a few minutes to loosen the dirt.
Once the time has passed, the roof is rinsed off using low-pressure water without causing damage. Again, professionals inspect the roof to ensure no residue or missed spots are left.
Benefits of Soft Wash Roof Cleaning
Soft wash roof cleaning offers several benefits, such as:
It protects shingles, tiles, or metal roofs from damage caused by high-pressure washing
It uses safe, biodegradable cleaning solutions that do not harm the surrounding landscaping, such as paint, gutters, plants
It removes algae, mildew, and moss, preventing them from growing back quickly
Soft pressure washing prevents roof damage, avoiding the need for expensive repairs or early roof replacement
It helps restore the look and appearance of your roof
It improves the longevity of your roof by removing moisture
Is Soft Washing Better Than Pressure Washing?
While pressure washing is a quick fix for cleaning roofs and is effective for removing stubborn dirt, soft washing always takes an edge over it. However time-consuming, it is safer and provides equally effective results.
Unlike pressure washing, which can cause damage to roofing materials, soft pressure washing is ideal for more delicate materials.
However, you can ask roofing experts for more tailored advice that aligns with your needs.
How Often Should You Soft Wash Your Roof?
Soft washing your roof is recommended every 1-3 years. However, the frequency depends on the following factors:
Living in a humid or rainy area might require frequent roof cleaning as compared to hot and dry climate regions
The type of roofing material influences how often one should soft wash their roofs. For instance, asphalt shingles require frequent cleaning compared to tiles or metal roofs
Visible dirt on your roof indicates that it is time to call professionals for roof cleaning
Extending your roof’s longevity might require more frequent cleaning than usual
Final Words
Soft wash roof cleaning is a gentle and effective method of cleaning roofs using low-pressure water combined with specialized cleaning solutions. Unlike traditional pressure washing, soft washing offers multiple benefits, such as protecting roofing material and surrounding landscaping, removing dirt, and improving your roof’s lifespan.
Get an estimate for soft wash roof cleaning at Everest Siding and Windows . Call us at (832) 334-2528 .

## What Is The Best Time to Replace Your Siding?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/what-is-the-best-time-to-replace-your-siding/
Updated: 2026-04-17
Summary: Learn why fall is the best time to schedule your siding installation project. Call us for more details on this.

What Is The Best Time to Replace Your Siding?
Apr 15, 2026
If your siding has aged well, you must consider replacing it. But did you know there is an ideal time for it?
Spring and fall are generally the best time of the year to replace your siding. In this blog, we will discuss why.
What Factors To Consider When Scheduling A Siding Installation
In this section, we will discuss some factors that can make it easy to decide when to invest in your siding installation.
What Siding Material Are You Using?
Considering your choice of material, some are easier to install at specific times of the year.
For example, vinyl expands in extremely hot weather and contracts in cold temperatures. So, installation scheduling is easier in moderate temperatures, such as early summer, spring or fall.
Fiber and wood stone are also often installed in midsummer and midwinter. If you are considering wood, installing it in drier seasons is best.
What Is Your Regional Weather Like?
While considering the choice of material, it is also best to consider your regional weather. Wet weather can deteriorate materials like wood and make it difficult to install siding quickly and easily.
It is best to wait until extreme weather settles down. We are talking about heavy downpours, too. If you live somewhere that experiences extreme winters, it is best to schedule your siding project for summer or fall.
Apart from Weather Conditions, How Can You Decide The Best Time?
In the first two points, we have discussed the weather entirely. However, that is just not it. Other factors can help you plan and schedule your siding installation in Houston, TX.
Do You Have Any Deadline?
Do you have any specific timeline to meet? Either you need to place your home on the market or complete the work before the family celebration that is coming up.
These things help you plan your siding installation in suitable weather, at least a few months ahead, ensuring that the project is completed before your personal commitments.
What Is Your Ideal Budget?
Budgeting for a siding replacement plays a role in choosing the best time. Fall is the ideal time to schedule new siding installation because material and labor costs are comparatively affordable. At that time of year, contractors are done with large-scale summer and spring projects, and the costs tend to go low.
If you are looking for subsidized prices, another best time to schedule siding replacements is when there are ongoing deals and discounts.
Why is Fall the Best Time for Siding Installation?
Autumn or fall weather is cool and moderate, ensuring materials undergo minimal contractions or expansions. During fall, no rains are expected, making it easier for professional siding experts to complete the project in time without worrying about material deterioration.
Not only that, prices tend to fall during this part of the year.
Overall Insight
In conclusion, the fall season is the best time to install siding. Moderate temperatures and dry conditions ensure a smoother installation process and maintain the integrity of the materials. Additionally, considering factors like your regional weather, project timelines, and budget can further guide your decision.
Experts at Everest Siding and Windows help you plan and choose the best time for siding installation in Houston, TX. Call us at (832) 334-2528 to book our services.

## What Type Of Roof Last The Longest?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/what-type-of-roof-last-the-longest/
Updated: 2024-08-08
Summary: Unsure about the roofing material best suited for your home? Consult us for best roofing material recommendations!

What Type Of Roof Last The Longest?
May 30, 2024
When it comes to choosing a long-lasting roofing material, homeowners are often faced with a multitude of options. It can also be overwhelming to decide the best kind of roofing material that will stand the test of time. In this blog, we will explore some of the best roofing materials that can provide both durability and longevity for our Houston based clients!
What Factors To Consider Before Choosing Any Roofing Material
If you are planning to invest on your roofing, here are some factors to take into consideration.
Regional weather and moisture levels
Design of your home and interior
Amount of routine maintenance
Quality of roofing material
Cost and budget
Common Materials Used For Roofing
In this section we have listed some of the commonly known roofing materials that will sustain the integrity of your homes over decades to come!
Clay Roofing: Clay material is considered to last between 30-50 years. It is however prone to damage but proper maintenance can likely increase its lifespan.
Slate Roofing: Slate is an ideal natural material for roofing. It is relatively expensive but can last over a lifetime. Considering its use in military wars helps us gauge its durability and strength.
Metal Roofing: Another common roofing material that will last you longest is metal. The life expectancy for these roofs range between 40-70 years. They are currently in style, durable and energy efficient.
Wood Shingles: Another classic example of roofing material is wood shingles. They can last over 30 years. It is important to consider routine maintenance, moisture control and debris accumulation before making a choice.
Composite Asphalt Roofing: Made up of organic or fiberglass material, asphalt shingles have not become a popular choice in roofing materials. They are cost effective, easy to maintain, durable and known for their strength. This roofing can last over 50 years.
Built-Up Roofs: They are alternating layers of roofing felt for flat roofs. Not only are they affordable, fire and moisture resistant, they can also last up to 20-30 years.
Which Is The Best Roofing Material For Your Home?
Considering the climate and residential patterns followed in Houston, TX, slate roofing is the best option. Slate is a form of stone which makes it resistant to damage including material deterioration, corrosion, insects, fire, or even water damage.
Apart from the durability benefits, it offers a stunning outlook for your home. To put it simply, slate roofs surpass both functional and aesthetic benefits for your roof.
Call For Professional Help!
In order to choose the right roofing material for your home, prioritizing durability, climate, compatibility and aesthetics and budget remains crucial. Thoroughly research your options, ask around neighbors or take professional advice.

## Why Airflow Behind Siding Matters in Humid Subtropical Climates
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/why-airflow-behind-siding-matters-in-humid-subtropical-climates/
Updated: 2026-09-23
Summary: Trapped moisture behind siding leads to mold and rot. Discover how airflow and rainscreen systems protect your home in humid climates.

Why Airflow Behind Siding Matters in Humid Subtropical Climates
Sep 15, 2026
A home in a humid subtropical climate faces heat, humidity, heavy rainfall, and long stretches of damp weather. Siding takes the brunt of these conditions, but what happens behind it often matters just as much.
Most wall assemblies don’t fail because the siding gives out. They fail when moisture slips past the surface and finds nowhere to go, which explains why some homes hold up for decades while others show problems within a few years.
How Trapped Moisture Damages Your Wall Assembly
After a heavy rain, some moisture is bound to work its way in through joints, penetrations, or small gaps, no matter how carefully the siding was installed. Even top-tier siding can’t stay fully waterproof under wind-driven rain. A water-resistive barrier, such as house wrap, acts as the drainage plane that sheds most of this water, but any moisture that gets past it still needs a way to dry.
That’s not the main concern. The bigger problem is what happens once moisture stays in the wall assembly. Mold, mildew, wood rot, and general material breakdown all become far more likely. Given enough time, trapped moisture weakens sheathing and fasteners, and it may even affect indoor air quality. Humid subtropical climates make the whole situation worse because the air rarely dries out enough to give the wall assembly a real chance to recover.
The Role of a Ventilated Rainscreen System
A rainscreen creates a ventilated gap between the siding and the water-resistive barrier, often formed with furring strips. This gap lets water drain and gives air room to travel vertically through the wall assembly.
As the sun warms the exterior, the air in the gap heats and rises, drawing in cooler air from below. That movement helps moisture evaporate faster than it would on its own. The wall assembly simply spends less time damp. This ongoing cycle, drying out again and again rather than staying wet, determines whether a wall assembly lasts.
Humid subtropical regions benefit from this more than most, since warm temperatures speed up biological growth and moisture damage. A wall assembly that dries well keeps paint and finishes looking better for longer, stretches out the siding’s usable life, reduces repairs tied to rot, staining, or mold, and helps protect the structural components behind the siding.
Even Without a Full Rainscreen, Airflow Products Add Protection
Not every homeowner installs a full rainscreen system. Homeowners can still add a ventilation product, such as Cor-A-Vent, as an extra layer of protection, provided it is compatible with the siding manufacturer’s installation guidelines.
A partial solution is less effective than a full rainscreen, but it still improves drainage and ventilation, which works well for renovations or budget-conscious builds. A full rainscreen isn’t always realistic in those cases, but some drainage and ventilation almost always is. Homeowners can also decide later whether upgrading to a full rainscreen is worthwhile.
The right approach comes down to a few things: the siding material, how much sun and rain the home actually takes on, and the local climate. A qualified contractor can walk through those factors and land on whether a full rainscreen or a more targeted airflow fix fits the project better.
Final Thoughts
Siding sheds water, but the wall assembly behind it needs a way to dry, and airflow handles that job. In a humid subtropical climate, designing for drainage and continuous airflow isn’t optional for a home that’s built to last.
Ready to build that protection into your next siding project? Call Everest Siding and Windows at (832) 334-2528 for a free consultation.

## Why are Sunrooms Better Than Traditional Home Additions?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/why-are-sunrooms-better-than-traditional-home-additions/
Updated: 2024-08-08
Summary: Want to know about the home addition for the sunrooms? Read our blog to know more about the traditional additions you look out for.

Why are Sunrooms Better Than Traditional Home Additions?
Jul 30, 2024
Adding more space to your home is always an exciting prospect. Whether you need an extra room for relaxation, entertaining, or simply enjoying the beauty of nature, choosing the right type of addition is crucial.
While traditional home additions have their benefits, sunrooms offer a unique and compelling alternative that can enhance your living experience in several ways. Here’s why sunrooms are often considered better than traditional home additions.
1. Connection with Nature
One of the most significant advantages of a sunroom is the seamless connection it provides with the outdoors. Traditional home additions, often designed with standard walls and windows, can feel enclosed and detached from nature.
Sunrooms, with their expansive glass walls, allow you to immerse yourself in the beauty of the outdoors while staying protected from the elements. Imagine sipping your morning coffee surrounded by the warmth of natural light, watching the seasons change from the comfort of your home, or stargazing at night without stepping outside.
2. Abundance of Natural Light
Natural light is known to have numerous benefits, including boosting mood, increasing productivity, and enhancing overall well-being. Sunrooms are designed to maximize sunlight exposure, creating a bright and cheerful space.
Unlike traditional additions, which may require artificial lighting during the day, sunrooms let in an abundance of natural light, reducing the need for electric lighting and potentially lowering your energy bills.
3. Versatility in Use
Sunrooms are incredibly versatile and can serve multiple purposes throughout the year. They can function as a cozy reading nook, a vibrant indoor garden, a home office, or a playroom for children.
The flexibility of a sunroom allows you to adapt the space to your changing needs without the constraints of a more permanent traditional addition. The possibilities are limited only by your imagination.
4. Enhanced Property Value
While any home addition can increase property value, sunrooms offer a unique selling point that can make your home stand out in the real estate market. Prospective buyers often appreciate the charm and functionality of a sunroom, seeing it as a desirable feature that enhances the overall appeal of the property.
The investment in a sunroom can yield significant returns if you decide to sell your home in the future.
5. Cost-Effective Construction
Sunrooms are generally more cost-effective to build than traditional home additions. The construction process is often quicker and less disruptive, requiring fewer materials and labor.
Additionally, because sunrooms are typically built with pre-fabricated materials and simpler designs, the overall cost can be significantly lower. This makes sunrooms an attractive option for homeowners looking to expand their living space without breaking the bank.
6. Energy Efficiency
Modern sunrooms are designed with energy efficiency in mind. High-quality, insulated glass and advanced framing materials help maintain a comfortable temperature year-round, reducing the need for excessive heating or cooling.
In contrast, traditional home additions may require extensive insulation and climate control systems to achieve similar energy efficiency, potentially leading to higher costs and maintenance.
7. Aesthetic Appeal
Sunrooms add a unique aesthetic appeal to your home. The airy, open design creates a visually stunning space that can be tailored to match your home’s architecture and interior design.
Whether you prefer a sleek, modern look or a more traditional style, a sunroom can be customized to complement your home’s overall aesthetic, enhancing its beauty and charm.
Final Words
While traditional home additions certainly have their place, sunrooms offer a distinctive and attractive alternative. If you’re considering expanding your home, a sunroom may be the perfect solution to create a bright, inviting space that you and your family can enjoy for years to come.
Consult our professional at Everest Siding and Windows to ensure your sunroom has a unique aesthetic. Call us today at (832) 334-2528 to schedule a consultation

## Why Choose Malarkey Roofing For Your Home?
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/why-choose-malarkey-roofing-for-your-home/
Updated: 2025-07-17
Summary: Learn why Malarkey Roofing is an ideal choice for homeowners. Know more about its eco-friendly materials, durability, and how it protects your home.

Why Choose Malarkey Roofing For Your Home?
Jul 15, 2025
When we talk about home protection, the roof plays an important role. It is not just an element that shields your home; it also enhances the overall value. By choosing the right roofing materials, you can have energy-efficient and durable roofing. However, with so many roofing solutions available, it can be hard for a person to choose the most reliable and functional roofing solution.
When we talk about roofing, Malarkey Roofing is a trusted name among homeowners. Known for its sustainability and quality, Malarkey is designed to last for a long time, even in the toughest conditions. In this blog, we will learn why choosing Malarkey Roofing is the ideal solution for homeowners. So, let’s begin!
What Is Malarkey Roofing?
Malarkey Roofing is a well-known manufacturer of high-quality roofing shingles. Founded in 1956, Malarkey has a reputation for developing advanced and durable roofing solutions. The company also stands out for its sustainable practices. They use upcycled rubber and plastic, along with shingles, to clean the air. With its focus on functionality and sustainability, Malarkey Roofing offers long-lasting protection to homeowners.
Reasons to Choose Malarkey Roofing
The following are some major reasons why homeowners choose Malarkey Roofing solutions:
Durability
Malarkey is designed to protect your home even in harsh weather conditions. This includes high winds, heavy rainfall, and hail. Its advanced formula will give your home strength and flexibility to withstand the toughest conditions.
Advanced Technology
Innovative features like polymer-modified asphalt and proprietary nailing are ideal for longevity. Many Malarkey shingles are of classes 3 and 4, which offer superior resistance in storms.
Eco-Friendly Materials
Being environmentally responsible has always been valuable for Malarkey. Made with upcycled materials like plastics and rubber, their shingles can reduce granules and help in cleaning the air, making your home sustainable.
Superior Protection
Malarkey offers limited lifetime coverage on different shingles. With their warranty, you can get insurance on manufacturing defects and get installation protection from contractors.
Attractive Styles
You can choose roofing solutions from a wide range of colors and architectural styles. You can choose a style that helps in enhancing the visual appeal of your home. From classic to modern designs, Malarkey has various exterior options.
Is Malarkey Right for Your Home?
Here are some situations where Malarkey Roofing is the ideal choice for you:
Harsh Weather Conditions: You live in an area with harsh weather conditions, which is why you need roofing solutions that are resistant to storms and high winds.
Long-Term Investment: Looking for high-performing roofing solutions that require low maintenance costs? Malarkey Roofing is the right choice for you.
Certified Products: If you are looking for roofing materials with proven certifications, then Maralerkey Roofing offers materials that are rated and certified by the Cool Roof Rating Council.
Final Thoughts
Malarkey Roofing is an ideal choice for homeowners who prioritize sustainability and visual appeal. Made with advanced technology and eco-friendly materials, Malarkey offers you roofing materials that are durable and perfect for long-term investment. At Everest Siding and Windows , you can choose the right roofing solution, the one that benefits your home. Contact us now at (832) 334-2528 and let our team help you in choosing the ideal roofing system according to your style and needs.

## Why Quality Latex Exterior Paint Is Worth the Investment
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/why-quality-latex-exterior-paint-is-worth-the-investment/
Updated: 2026-10-28
Summary: Quality latex exterior paint can improve coverage and weather resistance. Learn why it may cost less to maintain over time and what prep it needs.

Why Quality Latex Exterior Paint Is Worth the Investment
Oct 15, 2026
Many homeowners compare price first when they select exterior paint, but the upfront cost rarely reflects the total cost over time.
Sunlight, rain, humidity, wind, and seasonal temperature changes all act on a home’s exterior year after year. A coating that cannot withstand them is likely to need replacement sooner than expected. Although it costs more upfront, quality latex exterior paint often justifies the difference.
Better Coverage for a More Even Finish
Quality latex exterior paint typically uses higher-grade pigments and resins than budget products. Pigments supply the color and hide what lies underneath. Resins bind the pigments into a film that adheres to the surface.
Higher-grade ingredients may mean fewer coats, which can save labor on a large home. The benefit is clearest when the old paint has faded in patches, such as on the sunniest side of the house. It also shows when a light color covers a dark one.
Improved Resistance to Weather and Sunlight
A wall facing the afternoon sun endures conditions that most interior surfaces do not. Ultraviolet light can cause colors to fade, and moisture contributes to peeling and cracking over time.
The resins in quality latex formulations are designed to remain flexible as temperatures rise and fall. Because the dried film moves with the siding instead of resisting it, it is less likely to crack and lose its bond. Quality formulations also use pigments chosen for fade resistance, although performance varies by product.
Some products include additives that limit algae and mildew growth. This feature varies by formulation and is especially valuable in humid regions.
Longer-Lasting Exterior Protection
Paint serves a protective purpose in addition to a decorative one. Once a coating begins to fail, the surface beneath it is exposed to moisture and weather, and damage can spread. A durable coating can delay that failure. The paint’s performance still depends on how it is applied, since even a quality product protects poorly over dirt or loose paint.
Lower Maintenance Costs Over Time
A higher price per gallon is a reasonable concern for any homeowner. Over several years, though, a cheaper paint may cost more if it fades or peels sooner than expected and the exterior has to be painted again. Each new project brings another charge for materials, surface preparation, and labor.
A more durable paint can lengthen the time between projects, and that longer interval may bring the total cost below that of the budget option, even though the price per gallon is higher.
Quality Paint Requires Proper Preparation
New paint lasts longer on a clean, sound surface. The work often begins with washing the siding to remove dirt, chalky residue, and mildew. A drying period follows.
Crews then scrape or sand flaking paint and repair or replace damaged boards. They fill open seams around windows, doors, and trim with exterior-grade caulk. Where bare material or stains would show through the finish, crews apply primer first. Skipping these steps is a common cause of premature peeling.
A Practical Long-Term Investment
With quality latex exterior paint, a home can have a more even finish and stronger protection against the weather than budget products offer. Everest Siding and Windows helps homeowners choose the right paint and prepare the surface before the first coat. Call (832) 334-2528 to schedule a consultation.

## Why You Need Hurricane Doors and Windows
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/why-you-need-hurricane-doors-and-windows/
Updated: 2024-01-30
Summary: If you have lived in Houston for at least 10 years then you have felt the wrath of tropical storms spurred by hurricanes.

Why You Need Hurricane Doors and Windows
Aug 26, 2019
If you have lived in Houston for at least 10 years then you have felt the wrath of tropical storms spurred by hurricanes. The amount of rain and high winds that can roll through this region can flood so many people ride jet skis down 45, and that’s not a joke (Allison anyone?) However, if you are new to Houston or the gulf coast you may not understand the importance of hurricane windows and doors for your home. Whenever you are considering making a significant improvement to your home such as replacement windows – you really need to consider the possibility of a tropical storm or hurricane. Even a category 1 hurricane or low-level tropical storm can do serious damage to your home. Having hurricane windows and doors helps protect your home and there are several reasons why they are a necessity.
Hurricane Damage Dynamics
If you have never lived in a region prone to hurricanes, you may not take authorities advice to evacuate seriously when a storm is heading for Houston. However, keep in mind they evacuations are difficult and costly for a city, so they don’t just do it on a whim. If they are saying evacuate, it means there’s some serious danger headed for us. These storms bring a nasty cocktail of extreme weather and dump it on the gulf coast in a short amount of time. Excessive rainfall, storm surges, and winds exceeding 75mph come together and pose a grave danger.
While your home is protected by exterior walls, doors, and windows can be the most vulnerable to the extreme conditions. Regular windows can tolerate direct impact winds of up to 85mph, which equates to a Category 2 hurricane. However, constant winds of such speed can eventually compromise the seal on the windows and break them. Not to mention the gulf coast has seen Hurricanes the 3, 4 and 5 category levels, which obliterates regular windows and doors with the wind speeds up to 170mph. Even if your windows and doors survive the wind, it is the flying debris that causes the most damage and allows the winds to rush in and due to pressure, destroy the home from the inside out.
Hurricane windows and doors are designed to withstand the impact of both debris and wind from even the strongest category 5 storms. When it comes to protecting your home wouldn’t you want protection from the worst case scenario for peace of mind?
Plywood Just Isn’t A Practical Solution
Many people think that boarding up windows and doors with plywood is a sufficient cheap alternative to having the proper hurricane doors and windows in their home. This is a very burdensome project that has to be completed in a short time usually and leaves permanent damage to your home. Not only to you leave holes all over your home’s exterior but plywood isn’t cheap! An average home has about 14 windows and four doors; at about $25 a sheet, you just spent over $500 in plywood and screws. Here is the kicker, most stronger storms such as Hurricane Ike, rip that plywood right off and sends it flying. So there goes your money, and your house anyway.
It’s The Law
In some regions of our great Gulf Coast, the building codes require hurricane windows and doors be installed on homes in order to be in compliance. Even many insurance policies won’t cover a home in these regions without them. So if you are building a new home in one of these regions like Galveston, or even getting replacement windows – they must be hurricane doors or windows.
It Adds Value To Your Home
Even if your city ordinances don’t require it if hurricane windows boosted the value of your home while protecting it too, wouldn’t you do it? Anything that adds appreciation to your home is a worthy investment, especially when it protects it as well.
Some of the best Homeowner’s insurance policies can be quite costly when you live in a hurricane region. Because of this, you want to do everything you can to earn discounts on your policy and adding hurricane doors or windows can help earn the largest discounts.
Weather The Storm With Everest
Never overlook the power of hurricanes or even tropical storms, even if you lived here for years and never experienced this display, it only takes one time to learn – Just one. Protect your home with Everest hurricane windows and doors by scheduling a free consultation today.

## Window Season is Here
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/window-season-is-here/
Updated: 2024-12-24
Summary: Discover the perfect window for your home! Explore styles, materials, and colors to find the ideal blend of function and design.

Window Season is Here
Aug 27, 2019
Making A Decision
Style, glass, color and material… It can be confusing and hard to know what window is best for you. While style and color have a lot to do with your specific home, the material your new windows are made of may depend on more than aesthetics. Here is everything you need to know about vinyl windows.
Vinyl windows are impact resistant and usually the most inexpensive option whilst offering the best value.
Vinyl is made up of polyvinyl chloride (commonly known as PVC) which is how they are referred to in Europe and have been the mainstay for new and replacement windows since the early 80’s in most of Europe. This material can expand and contract. If this is the case, why would I opt for vinyl windows, other than the fact they are a bit cheaper?
With the proper installer, these windows can be a very good option. Be sure to ask your installer if they plan on using foam to fill the frame’s cavities. Also, be sure to ask for heat-welded (fusion) corners which will prohibit air leakage as well. With proper installation, vinyl windows are great thermal insulators which means, they are energy efficient and will save you money on your energy bills! Because they are made from PVC, they are also very pliable. They can be molded into nearly any shape which makes them very customizable. PVC also allows vinyl windows to be low maintenance. They do not scratch or dent, and they are easy to clean. Just some soap and water will do the trick! DO NOT waste money on special vinyl window cleaner products from stores, they can in a lot of cases actually do more harm than good by miniature scratches being formed on the surface of the vinyl, which then takes away from the appeal.
Green conscious? Vinyl windows are recyclable! They can be melted and remolded into new products! Even scraps from the manufacturing process of other vinyl windows can be recycled. WORD OF CAUTION>> some budget vinyl windows are made from recycled products, do not invest in these windows, they will eventually discolor and warp. Insist of virgin vinyl as a bare minimum, ideally, go with enhanced polymers but settle for no less than virgin vinyl.
Because premier window companies have made huge advancements in vinyl window manufacturing, vinyl is now more durable than ever. Today, new vinyl replacement windows can handle large pieces of glass, like in picture windows, with ease. Vinyl is now more weather resistant than ever before ensuring they will be durable and long lasting in any climate. We will visit the differences in glass packages at a later date.
Vinyl windows will never need scraping, staining or painting. This will save you time and money on routine maintenance.
Moisture can cause a lot of damage to any window or window area. Condensation is limited with vinyl windows due to their energy efficient structure. Vinyl windows have a high condensation resistance factor, or CRF, which means it will happen far less often with your vinyl windows than other materials. However condensation is a fact of nature so whilst it will be minimized, please don’t be shocked at the occasional condensation, predominantly happens at a set dew point, and will often be on the outside!!
Want a more modern style instead of traditional? Then vinyl is your best bet. It’s sleek and clean looking; much more streamlined than a wood window.
If you’re selling your home soon, new windows are a great way to increase the value of your home. It is one less thing someone moving has to add to the list of “to-do’s” in their new home. Vinyl replacement windows are most certainly a value-added feature when selling your home.
In conclusion, if your top priorities are finding an inexpensive, energy efficient and maintenance free window, vinyl replacement windows are for you!
We offer a free no We offer a free no obligation in-home demonstration and our proposal is always good for 12 months.

## Winterizing Your Home in Houston, TX
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/winterizing-your-home-in-houston-tx/
Updated: 2024-01-30
Summary: Getting your home ready for the colder months isn’t something you usually look forward to year after year

Winterizing Your Home in Houston, TX
Aug 26, 2019
Stay Warm & Cozy at Home
Getting your home ready for the colder months isn’t something you usually look forward to year after year, but it’s an essential step to take in order to prevent costly damage and repairs. Here’s how you can winterize your windows and siding to protect your home during the winter months.
Preparing Your Windows
Weather stripping can be the difference between drafty and sealed windows. Foam-based stripping that is fully intact will keep any drafts out throughout the cooler months.
In addition, check if your windows are held in place with glazing. Many older windows have this glazing, which is unfortunately prone to cracking or breaking. The simple solution is to clean out any loose glazing and apply silicone caulk in its place. This will seal the glass and eliminate any drafts. You can also install window installation film, which looks and feels similar to shrink wrap.
If your windows are outdated, it may be a good idea to replace them now. Storm windows are an excellent update to make, and they can add value and energy efficiency to your home. Everest Siding And Windows has a variety of impact-resistant vinyl windows for you to choose from.
Winterizing Your Siding
Checking your siding for any shifting or cracking is always a good place to start. If you do happen to find any damage to your home’s siding, it’s crucial to repair or replace it before the temperatures get any lower.
As an extra step, installing extra insulation is never a bad idea. It can act as another barrier to keep the chill of the cooler winter season out and protect your home from the elements.
Your gutters work hand in hand with your siding to protect your home, but if they aren’t cleaned properly, they can cause extreme water damage to your siding. Make sure your gutters are cleaned out to prevent this from occurring.
Contact Us
Need some help preparing your home for winter? Our family-owned and –operated company is here to make sure your home stays safe and warm throughout the season. If you live in Houston, TX and you’re looking forward to the cooler months, give us a call today!

## Privacy Policy
URL: https://everestsidingandwindows.com/privacy-policy/
Updated: 2024-12-23
Summary: Read Everest Siding and Windows' Privacy Policy to understand how we protect your information and ensure your privacy is respected.

Privacy Policy
Welcome to Everest Siding And Windows . We are dedicated to protecting your privacy and safeguarding your personally identifiable information. Our privacy policy explains how we handle the personal information we collect from you through our website, service interactions, and other channels. Our practices are guided by key privacy principles and legislation, ensuring that we respect your privacy rights.
1. Our Commitment to Your Privacy
Everest Siding And Windows is committed to protecting the privacy of our customers. We understand the importance of privacy and are dedicated to ensuring the security and confidentiality of your personal information. This policy outlines our practices regarding the collection, use, and sharing of your information.
2. Information We Collect:
Registration Information:
To access certain features of our services, you may need to register. During registration, we may ask for personal information such as your name, contact details, and other relevant information to enhance your service experience.
IP Addresses and Cookies:
We collect IP addresses to understand how our services are used and to tailor experiences to your needs. Cookies are used to personalize your interaction with our website, remembering your preferences and login information.
3. How We Collect Your Information:
Your information is collected directly through our website interactions, service registrations, and communications. We may also receive information from third-party sources that you have authorized to share with us.
4. Use of Your Information:
We use the information collected to improve our services, understand customer preferences, provide personalized experiences, and communicate with you about services, promotions, and updates you may find valuable. We analyze this data to enhance the usability and features of our services.
5. Protecting Your Information: We do not share your information with any third parties. Our commitment to protecting your privacy is paramount, and we ensure the confidentiality and security of your personal data at all times. We do not sell, rent, or otherwise disclose your information to outside parties. Information will only be disclosed if absolutely required by law or in the good faith belief that such action is necessary to comply with legal processes or to protect and defend the rights and property of Everest Siding And Windows.
6. Your Privacy Controls:
You have control over your personal information. You can access, update, or request deletion of your information by contacting us. We also provide options to control the receipt of marketing communications and the use of cookies through your browser settings.
7. Protection of Children’s Privacy:
We do not knowingly collect information from children under the age of 13. If we become aware of such collection, we will take steps to remove the information and comply with relevant laws.
8. Security Measures:
We employ robust security measures to protect your information from unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction. Our security practices include encryption, firewalls, and secure server facilities.
9. Changes to Our Privacy Policy:
Our Privacy Policy may be updated from time to time to reflect changes in our practices or legal obligations. We encourage you to review our policy periodically for the latest information on our privacy practices.
10. Contact Us:
If you have any questions about our privacy practices or wish to update your information, please contact us at:
Email: info@everestsidingandwindows.com
Phone: (832) 334-2528
Address: 11424 Spring Cypress Rd Unit A1, Tomball, TX 77377, United States
Your privacy is important to us at Everest Siding And Windows. We strive to manage your personal information transparently, responsibly, and securely. Thank you for trusting us with your siding & window needs.
